Hey folks,
I joined **The Left Hook** this week, and we did not hold back. We dug into Trump's State of the Union chaos, the Epstein fallout, ICE overreach, and the identity crisis inside the Democratic Party. This wasn't cable news spin -- it was a real, unfiltered conversation about where the country is and whether we're actually ready for what's coming next.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:21**] I make the case that Trump has "unified" the country -- just not the way he thinks. Independents are fleeing. His numbers are collapsing. Even three-time Trump voters (yes, my parents) are done tuning in.
* [**00:03:40**] We get personal about why people still voted for Trump -- inflation, distrust, Biden's age -- and what Democrats refuse to learn from it.
* [**00:07:01**] What does Trump even run on tonight? We break down the gaslighting playbook, the tariff chaos, and why leaning on the stock market won't save him.
* [**00:14:22**] The Democratic civil war: progressive vs. "moderate," righteous anger vs. electability. I explain why I care about winning first -- and why that tension isn't going away.
* [**00:40:30**] I lay out what I actually believe Democrats should run on: break the Epstein class, go big on anti-corruption, confront AI-driven economic disruption, and stop pretending small tweaks will meet this moment.

This episode is about strategy -- but it's also about values. About whether we're going to nibble at the edges while the ground shifts under us, or actually meet this moment with the scale it demands. We don't agree on everything. That's the point. But we agree the stakes are enormous. And if you value honest conversations like this -- the kind that don't dodge the hard parts -- help me keep them going.

body:
We can win this -- but not without your support
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260227-2562)
Peter,
We got amazing news this week: Fran is in _first place_ for the second poll in a row from Marquette Law School!
We're thrilled, but not surprised. Fran's been hitting the ground all across the state sharing her message of permanent affordability in cities, towns, meeting halls and dive bars. And the same scenario plays out again and again: People come to our events a little wary, a little skeptical, but after hearing Fran's thoughtful and deep approach to policy, they jump onboard with enthusiasm. Once they get to know her, even a little bit, they're all in.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260227.6UkJkJ&refcode=em20260227-2562&t=1&akid=2562%2E105371%2EiIV3tP)
As a team, we recognize that "all-in" feeling, because we feel it too. We're working for Fran because we believe deeply in her work and her commitment. We know she's a generational candidate, and we're going to do all we can to support her.
This weekend, Fran and I are on the road to Oshkosh, Green Bay, Sheboygan, Appleton, Ashland and Rice Lake. That's a huge tour of the northern part of the state! We just keep going, because we know that work is one of the big things that sets Fran apart.
We have 2,000 volunteers eager to share why they support this campaign. We have volunteer-led social events, policy discussions, and fundraisers all over the state. And soon we'll be getting out on doors, talking neighbor-to-neighbor about Fran's vision for a better Wisconsin.
But all these things (the travel, the campaign literature, the events, the staff) cost money. A lot of money.
Fran's leading in the polls, but in order to stay competitive, we have to raise more funds. Please don't let Fran's message for permanent affordability die out because we can't afford to share it!
Whether you can chip in $5, $50, $500, or $5000, every contribution keeps this campaign alive and allows us to get the word out to more voters.
**[Please donate now, so we can fill up the gas tank up north!](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260227.6UkJkJ&refcode=em20260227-2562&t=2&akid=2562%2E105371%2EiIV3tP)**
Thanks for all you do!
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260227.6UkJkJ&amount=5&refcode=em20260227-2562&t=21&akid=2562%2E105371%2EiIV3tP)**
With gratitude,
— Becky Cooper, Campaign Manager

My opponent's approval rating is underwater and sinking fast. You could say his numbers are sleeping with the fishes... Take it from me: Alaskans are tired of politicians and their corporate donors getting richer while things get tougher here at home. We’ve had enough of skyrocketing health care costs and out-of-control grocery prices (up to $17 for a gallon of milk!), all while DC people look after their own wallets and stock portfolios. But here’s the thing: When dark money donors see these numbers and realize that we have what it takes to win this Senate seat and shut that system down, they’re going to spend big to try and stop us. We can’t afford to become complacent. Not when the stakes are this high, and not when our runway is this short. So we have to keep building on this momentum in order to build the grassroots movement we need to win. I’m a first-time candidate, virtually unknown to most Minnesotans outside my service record. The Democrat machine will dump tens of millions to hold this seat and push their agenda. I can’t self-fund, and I won’t back down. That’s where you come in. Together, we will: Secure the border: Welcome legal immigrants who love America; deport criminals and stop the chaos. Revive our economy: Cut wasteful spending, unleash energy independence, and restore dignity for working Minnesotans. Empower parents: Put them back in control of education, not bureaucrats or radicals. Defend the Constitution: Every word, every right—no compromises. I’ve carried our flag into the fight before. I’ve seen what it stands for. And I will never stop defending it—for Minnesota, for our kids, for a stronger, prouder America. subject: Honor Black History, Defend Voting Rights
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM1MTY5NjIS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQwMDg3NTMyOQS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
This Black History Month in America’s 250th year, I’ve been reflecting on the
centuries-long path to secure voting rights for Black Americans. With President
Trump, MAGA Republicans, and their billionaire backers trying to dismantle our
democracy, this is history we need to be paying attention to. In fact, right now, Trump and Republicans are seeking to imperil the voting rights that generations
of Black activists and others fought to achieve. They’re pushing three similar anti-voter bills https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/x_ : the so-called SAVE Act, SAVE America Act, and Make Elections Great Again (MEGA) Act, two of which have already passed the Republican-controlled House of
Representatives. If made into law, these bills would unravel hard-won access to
the ballot box for millions of eligible voters. One of the biggest lessons I think we can learn from the history of voting
rights in the United States is that it’s not enough to only pass laws that
protect our freedoms. We have to keep fighting for them. So, how did we get here? It’s no secret that when the United States was founded, most Americans couldn’t
vote. A patchwork of laws generally limited participation in our democracy to
White, male Christians who owned land. The religion and landowning pieces fell
away within a generation, but the White male part persisted. It took the blood, sweat, and tears of many generations to achieve the voting
rights and protections Americans have today. The Civil War was the bloodiest war
in U.S. history, but it led to the ratification of the 13th Amendment, which
ended slavery; the 14th Amendment, which guarantees equal protection of the law
and due process regardless of race, and birthright citizenship to those born in
the United States; and the 15th Amendment, which bans racial discrimination in
voting. But a decade after the Civil War, amid widespread terrorist violence against
freed Black Americans, a racist Supreme Court striking down civil rights laws,
and with a weary White public ready to move on, the promises of the 14th and
15th Amendments — including Black voting rights — were broken. For nearly a century after the U.S.ended slavery and amended the Constitution to
protect Black voting rights, generations of Black Americans still couldn’t vote.
During this Jim Crow era, White Southern politicians, judges, prosecutors,
juries, law enforcement, and vigilantes repressed Black Americans with lawless
violence and intimidation. If Black Americans tried to vote or register, White
mobs could lynch them for it. There would be no repercussions for the
perpetrators of these horrific crimes: cops would not stop them, prosecutors
would not charge them, and juries would not convict them. In addition to
institutionalized violence, Jim Crow states came up with racist loopholes like
“grandfather clauses” — literally, a person could only vote if their grandfather
could vote. With the legacy of slavery and ongoing Jim Crow, the chance that
anyone’s Black grandfather had been able to vote was essentially impossible.
Both Congress and the Supreme Court looked the other way. During the Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s and 1960s, there was still Jim
Crow violence, suppression, and intimidation, and even Dr. Martin Luther King
Jr. was not popular with White America during his time. When John Lewis and
others marched across the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama, to protest for
voting rights, they were savagely beaten by White law enforcement. The Voting Rights Act of 1965 was made possible by the unrelenting work,
sacrifice, and heroism of Black Civil Rights activists. This includes activists many know and revere, like Dr. King, John Lewis, and
Rosa Parks, as well as hundreds of thousands of everyday people of all races who
believed in the cause of freedom, and knew that to achieve it, they’d have to
fight for it. Their activism, coupled with the power of Black voters in the North, the efforts
of pro-Civil Rights politicians like President Lyndon Johnson, and a briefly
liberal Supreme Court led by Chief Justice Earl Warren, set the stage for the
most successful civil rights law in American history. It was only possible
because everyday people organized, mobilized, and held their leaders
accountable. And when the Voting Rights Act of 1965 became law, the United
States of America finally achieved a true multiracial democracy for the first
time. But over the past 13 years, an increasingly far-right Supreme Court majority has
been chipping away at the landmark Voting Rights Act. Republican politicians in
the states have taken advantage of the current Supreme Court to disenfranchise
Black voters with alarming precision. LCV has long stood with nearly every
Democrat in Congress in supporting legislation to repair the Voting Rights Act,
but nearly every Republican in Congress stands against it. And even now, the
MAGA Justices on the Supreme Court are considering striking down what’s left of
the Voting Rights Act in a case called Louisiana v. Callais. All in addition to the anti-voter SAVE Act, SAVE America Act and Make Elections Great Again (MEGA) Act. These threats to voting rights, racial justice, and democracy are
interconnected. Today, the Department of Homeland Security agents — including
ICE and CBP — who use violence against people, illegally violate our due process
rights, and target people of color walk in the footsteps of the former
Confederate soldiers who terrorized the freedmen and the people of conscience
who stood alongside them after the Civil War. They follow in the footsteps of
the cops who brutalized John Lewis and others on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. And
when the president associated with a violent mob attacking our Capitol on
January 6th returns to office, pardons the people who carried out that violence,
and weaponizes the Justice Department to weaken civil rights and persecute
political opponents, we should remember the century of Jim Crow in which
violent, lawless White supremacy ruled huge parts of our country. It’s up to us, the people of the United States, to ensure that leaders of good
conscience hold power in our government.We have to protect the rule of law, counter abuses of power, and shore up the
integrity of our institutions. Democracy relies on our participation, so when
you see messages in your inbox from me or my LCV colleagues, I hope you’ll join
us in taking action. Generations of Black activists put everything on the line to secure equal rights
including the right to vote, which protects all other rights. Let’s honor their
legacy, and protect our future, by working to keep elections free and fair — for
all Americans. Sincerely, Doug Lindner

Dear Friend,

Every day at Willowdale Ranch, we meet veterans and first responders who carry more than most people will ever see. Some arrive quiet and guarded. Some arrive exhausted from years of holding everything together. And some arrive simply looking for a place where they can breathe again. What we have learned is this: when people are given space, compassion, and the healing power of the outdoors, something inside them begins to lift. Hope returns. Shoulders drop. Hearts open. That is the work happening at Willowdale Ranch.

Willowdale was created for a higher purpose. Our mission is to serve those who have served, to lift up veterans and first responders carrying unseen burdens, and to offer a place where the land itself becomes part of the healing process. Time outdoors, shared work, fellowship, and quiet moments of peace can begin to restore what life has worn down.

One of the most powerful parts of our work is our equine-assisted learning. Horses have a unique ability to reach people in ways that words cannot. Their calm presence and intuitive nature create a safe space for veterans and first responders to rebuild trust, confidence, and emotional grounding. Many who arrive carrying stress or trauma find that working with our horses becomes a turning point in their healing journey.

As Willowdale continues to grow, we are inviting those who believe in this mission to stand with us. Your support helps create a sanctuary where healing is not just hoped for, but experienced.

clean_body: <> View this email in a browser Dear Friend, Every day at Willowdale Ranch, we meet veterans and first responders who carry more than most people will ever see. Some arrive quiet and guarded. Some arrive exhausted from years of holding everything together. And some arrive simply looking for a place where they can breathe again. What we have learned is this: when people are given space, compassion, and the healing power of the outdoors, something inside them begins to lift. Hope returns. Shoulders drop. Hearts open. That is the work happening at Willowdale Ranch. Willowdale was created for a higher purpose. Our mission is to serve those who have served, to lift up veterans and first responders carrying unseen burdens, and to offer a place where the land itself becomes part of the healing process. Time outdoors, shared work, fellowship, and quiet moments of peace can begin to restore what life has worn down. One of the most powerful parts of our work is our equine-assisted learning. Horses have a unique ability to reach people in ways that words cannot. Their calm presence and intuitive nature create a safe space for veterans and first responders to rebuild trust, confidence, and emotional grounding. Many who arrive carrying stress or trauma find that working with our horses becomes a turning point in their healing journey. As Willowdale continues to grow, we are inviting those who believe in this mission to stand with us. Your support helps create a sanctuary where healing is not just hoped for, but experienced. <> $600 Yearly Membership <> $50 Monthly IRON HORSE MEMBERSHIP For those who carry the mission further. body:
Help us close out February strong so we can head into March ready to win.

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/lq1-ahnpoW_BvBjD9F-9UA~~/AAUS1hA~/6g8AJlSNQpo6Te2ALw9Zu3PmLnY_ZbFVg4ARypqYwDacv-J5IrO3oeRzxDFUmsF5dWCKEQTiH_HYKQnKdVyavtAz-GuuEw6kowguOasE7pCXHI6tBQUX-No2_3Ghndsc)
| | [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/NbbFhJBDyr4BOY2LrHsUkw~~/AAUS1hA~/tnsqGPI1RLJhC5mzTDvIeEKrDcEIYTl9gl_v_jPCWfz_yVf_pWa8wL_0ZrvJuLnZkhABz3Jay7oHt9N9WwX7zmZ1H8kjDA1qsPhnCPnhttvBw6gLRECPhIK4JtczwTLnxo3UPqsIZEdKZ826CrvGqg~~) **Friend,** I’ve spent years driving across this district and put over **15,000 miles on our family vehicle in the last ten months.** Town halls. Living rooms. Farms. Machine shops. Small businesses. I’ve listened to parents worried about healthcare costs. Seniors stretched thin on fixed incomes. Farmers dealing with water scarcity. Working families doing everything right and still falling behind. And the frustration is real. Because while we are grinding it out every day... **She’s using us for her own personal political gain.** And this should not surprise anyone. Lauren Boebert has shown us time and time and time again exactly who she is. She has failed Colorado. She has failed our country. She represents everything that is wrong with our political system. **Political theater over policy. Ego over service. Noise over results.** While we are asking for solutions, she is chasing headlines.
While we need serious leadership, she delivers embarrassment.
While families struggle, she blocks meaningful legislation. **We deserve better.** We deserve someone who knows our communities. Who understands our struggles. Who has lived them. Who will fight for us in Washington instead of humiliating us. **That is why I am running for Congress.** Hard working families have been abandoned for far too long. We need equitable, meaningful change. And I will not stop fighting until that happens. Now I need to ask for your help. We are just short of our February fundraising goal. Many of you have already stepped up and I am deeply grateful. But to close this month strong and head into March with real momentum, we need one final push. And here’s the truth. **I refuse corporate cash.**
**I refuse to call lobbyists.**
**I refuse to beg dark money super PACs.** That means this campaign runs on working people. If we are going to defeat Lauren Boebert, it will not be because insiders funded it. **It will be because you did.** If you believe Colorado deserves serious leadership...

Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections.
That's why they create bills like the SAVE and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote.
Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=022726_4&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NYT: Trump Leans on Congress to Address His False Claims of Voter Fraud [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=022726_4&amount=25]
President Trump used his State of the Union address to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address his often-repeated -- and equally often debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud.
The SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms.
This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=022726_4&amount=35]
Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd-party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=022726_4&amount=35]

How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results.
For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters.
Reuters has a fuller accounting in recent reporting. Florida, for example, spent millions investigating voter fraud and creating a new state department to oversee election security. They've only prosecuted two non-citizens for voting since 2022. North Carolina said they found nine non-citizens registered to vote out of 7.7 million voters. Utah recently investigated their entire voter roll of 2.1 million registered voters and found one registered non-citizen who never attempted to vote.
The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. "
Team, the lies aren't going to stop, but we can push back and make sure bills like this abomination never pass. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to stand against voter suppression bills in Congress and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=022726_4&amount=35]

clean_body: Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections. That's why they create bills like the SAVE and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote. Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [] Voter Action Project [] NYT: Trump Leans on Congress to Address His False Claims of Voter Fraud [] President Trump used his State of the Union address to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address his often-repeated -- and equally often debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud. The SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks. PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE ACT NOW ➜ [] Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including: Registration by mail 3rd-party voter registration drives Online voter registration in states that allow it Automatic voter registration Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities. “ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ” Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [] If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [] GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [] OTHER AMOUNT [] How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results. For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters. Reuters has a fuller accounting in recent reporting. Florida, for example, spent millions investigating voter fraud and creating a new state department to oversee election security. They've only prosecuted two non-citizens for voting since 2022. North Carolina said they found nine non-citizens registered to vote out of 7.7 million voters. Utah recently investigated their entire voter roll of 2.1 million registered voters and found one registered non-citizen who never attempted to vote. The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. " Team, the lies aren't going to stop, but we can push back and make sure bills like this abomination never pass. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to stand against voter suppression bills in Congress and beyond >> [] [] [] [] [] [] Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities. Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? name: Sen. Chris Murphy
subject: Gina Hinojosa
body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Let’s talk about Texas.
All eyes are on the Lone Star State right now ahead of Tuesday’s primaries. Even Donald Trump is in Corpus Christi for an event today because he knows Texas is critical to the midterms.
So I want to share why I’m supporting Gina Hinojosa for governor and reaching out in the hopes that you will do the same as she takes on Greg Abbott and his $106 million war chest.
The good news is — despite the resource and name ID disadvantage — recent polling already shows her down by just 3%. Abbott 46% - Hinojosa 43%. That’s an extremely close starting point against a Republican incumbent in Texas.
**[So please, if you care about Democrats winning Texas, make a contribution to Gina Hinojosa’s campaign for governor.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260227_5_murphy.xUMTjB&refcode=em20260227-673&t=1&akid=673%2E299639%2EQoq-t3)**
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260227_5_murphy.QNVooS&amount=5&refcode=em20260227-673&t=2&akid=673%2E299639%2EQoq-t3)
Gina will make an excellent governor. She’s a daughter of the Rio Grande Valley who became a civil rights lawyer. She has been a leader first on the Austin school board and now in the Texas State House.
And most importantly, she is a fighter for the people. Since day one, she has called out Greg Abbott’s corruption — giving billions of taxpayer dollars to the billionaires and corporations who bankroll his campaigns.
There’s a reason he has a $106 million war chest — allowing him to be on the air already trying to salvage his unpopular reputation. Billionaires and corporate donors love him. He’s proven he will sell out working people in a heartbeat to line the pockets of the 1%.
Yes, Democrats have longed for years to flip the state back, and I believe this could be the year. We are going to have incredible candidates like Gina at the top of the ticket.
Imagine the rebuke it would be to Donald Trump’s attempt to rig the midterms — starting with redrawing Texas’ Congressional maps — if we flipped the whole damn state.
I’m putting skin in the game and sending a donation to Gina as well. So I’m asking you to do the same and give what you can:
**[Please make a contribution to Gina Hinojosa’s campaign for governor. Do it today to send a powerful message — while Donald Trump is in Texas — that we’re putting an end to his corruption.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260227_5_murphy.QNVooS&refcode=em20260227-673&amount=5&t=3&akid=673%2E299639%2EQoq-t3)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260227_5_murphy.QNVooS&amount=5&refcode=em20260227-673&t=22&akid=673%2E299639%2EQoq-t3)
Every best wish,
Chris Murphy

Today I flew home from Israel.
It wasn't a trip for a social media boost (and definitely not a free trip of the Israeli government).
Before I went to my gate, I had a conversation with a woman sitting near me -- visibly disheartened. A UK citizen born in Iran, she had been denied entry into Israel. She had come to visit close Israeli friends and their children. She arrived with gifts in her suitcase and hope in her heart -- and instead was put back on a plane to the UK.
_We are not here to examine the issue or feed into a Tucker Carlson fantasy about Israeli passport control that was a non-issue._
Here's what struck me most:
She is not an enemy of Israel. She is an Iranian-born woman who openly supports Israel and she has many Jewish friends in Israel, the UK and the US. She spoke about her love of the Jewish people and her deep relationships with Christians in the UK. She shared that she was required to declare herself Muslim on official documents -- though that was not the faith of her upbringing.
We spoke about the many Jews in Israel and America who support the Iranian people and long for an Iran free from the Ayatollahs. _There was no hostility in her heart -- only disappointment._
Trying to lighten the moment, I told her that the Jewish people tend to make you earn entry everywhere and rejection is part of our DNA -- and that if she were converting to Judaism, she would likely face a lot of rejection from rabbis before being accepted. We laughed.
Before boarding, she gave her gifts -- meant for her friends' children -- to an airport employee so some joy could still come from the trip. _**That small act said more about her character than any passport stamp ever could.**_
And then a thought struck me.
Perhaps she was denied not because she was unwanted -- but because someone quietly calculated risk that had nothing to do with her heritage.
Earlier in the week, when someone asked when I was flying home, I joked: "**Friday ... Iran permitting.**" The Israelis around me laughed and all were convinced that I was not getting out.
_**What if her three-day visit was viewed through that same lens?**_
_**What if the escalating situation made even a short stay too uncertain?**_
Perhaps they denied her knowing she was coming for a long weekend and wanted to spare her from being stranded during an unpredictable escalation?
That denial may have been a blessing. Only time will tell. I told her that she may look back later at this and laugh at this inconvenience.
Sometimes a closed gate is an open shield.
**The Ripple Effects of Crisis**
These global crises -- whether it is the death and ongoing siege of the Druze, Christians, and other minorities in Syria without adequate humanitarian aid, the massacres of Christians in Nigeria, or the deaths of protesting Iranians -- carry consequences far beyond headlines.
Some consequences are physical: Death. Displacement. Child trafficking. Rape. Torture. Imprisonment.
Others are emotional and psychological: Hurt. Fear. Trauma. PTSD that will never receive adequate treatment.
Not all victims bleed in public.
Sometimes the price of geopolitical conflict is paid quietly -- in airport terminals, in denied visas, in family separations, in unanswered prayers.
**Conversations Matter**
Despite the disappointment, something meaningful happened.
Two strangers from very different backgrounds found common ground (_other than a love for Albaloo polo - a Persian sour cherry rice dish served with Kebabs_) -- a shared belief in freedom, faith, dignity, and hope for a better future for both Israel and the Iranian people.
We need more of these conversations -- especially while diplomacy moves at a pace that feels unacceptable to those living with the consequences.
**A Deeper Conviction**
I head home with a deeper love for Israel.
Call me extreme. Call me a radical Zionist. I will wear it as a badge of honor.
But loving Israel does not weaken my love for America. It strengthens it. **Being America First means understanding alliances, values, and the strategic importance of standing with democratic partners.**
I was in Judea and Samaria. I stood at sites where Jews were murdered simply for being Jewish. I learned about out-of-the-box solutions designed to deter future terror. _**The threats are real. The stakes are high.**_
Israel benefits from a strong American partnership and Ambassador Mike Huckabee as a modern day Maccabee. _I believe he will go on to be the most important US Ambassador to Israel in my lifetime._ And the United States benefits from an Israel that is secure, stable, and resilient.
Freedom is costly.
Sometimes the cost is paid in blood.
Sometimes it is paid in tears or a temporary broken heart that will mend.
And sometimes it is paid in quiet acts of resilience -- like a woman giving away gifts in an airport so disappointment does not have the final word.
The price of freedom is high.
But surrender is higher.

Earlier in the week, when someone asked when I was flying home, I joked: "Friday ... Iran permitting." The Israelis around me laughed and all were convinced that I was not getting out. What if her three-day visit was viewed through that same lens? What if the escalating situation made even a short stay too uncertain? Perhaps they denied her knowing she was coming for a long weekend and wanted to spare her from being stranded during an unpredictable escalation? That denial may have been a blessing. Only time will tell. I told her that she may look back later at this and laugh at this inconvenience. Sometimes a closed gate is an open shield. The Ripple Effects of Crisis These global crises -- whether it is the death and ongoing siege of the Druze, Christians, and other minorities in Syria without adequate humanitarian aid, the massacres of Christians in Nigeria, or the deaths of protesting Iranians -- carry consequences far beyond headlines. Some consequences are physical: Death. Displacement. Child trafficking. Rape. Torture. Imprisonment. Others are emotional and psychological: Hurt. Fear. Trauma. PTSD that will never receive adequate treatment. Not all victims bleed in public. Sometimes the price of geopolitical conflict is paid quietly -- in airport terminals, in denied visas, in family separations, in unanswered prayers. Conversations Matter Despite the disappointment, something meaningful happened. Two strangers from very different backgrounds found common ground (other than a love for Albaloo polo - a Persian sour cherry rice dish served with Kebabs) -- a shared belief in freedom, faith, dignity, and hope for a better future for both Israel and the Iranian people. We need more of these conversations -- especially while diplomacy moves at a pace that feels unacceptable to those living with the consequences. A Deeper Conviction I head home with a deeper love for Israel. Call me extreme. Call me a radical Zionist. I will wear it as a badge of honor. But loving Israel does not weaken my love for America. It strengthens it. Being America First means understanding alliances, values, and the strategic importance of standing with democratic partners. I was in Judea and Samaria. I stood at sites where Jews were murdered simply for being Jewish. I learned about out-of-the-box solutions designed to deter future terror. The threats are real. The stakes are high.** Israel benefits from a strong American partnership and Ambassador Mike Huckabee as a modern day Maccabee. I believe he will go on to be the most important US Ambassador to Israel in my lifetime. And the United States benefits from an Israel that is secure, stable, and resilient. Freedom is costly. Sometimes the cost is paid in blood. Sometimes it is paid in tears or a temporary broken heart that will mend. And sometimes it is paid in quiet acts of resilience -- like a woman giving away gifts in an airport so disappointment does not have the final word. The price of freedom is high. But surrender is higher. | A guest post by| Consultant, Political Consultant, Campaign Manager, Construction Consultant and Corporate Attorney. # they're trying to sneak an anti-ICE bill through
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Feb 28
---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
This morning, a bill passed out of committee that read to me like an anti-ICE bill in disguise...
[Watch + read why here](https://substack.com/redirect/63a127c2-e4f7-4384-a6a3-0f03fbf1b3c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d6ab3b15-c406-4407-9899-2df6152d33b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Ok, you back? Good!**
Now, email and call Senators Kelly Anthon and Lori Den Hartog and tell them to let this bill die the death it deserves.
It's not complicated, it's not ambiguous, it's just bad policy dressed up in language designed to make you feel fine about it. Senators Anthon and Den Hartog need to hear from you before they decide that silence means approval.

we are being told that another catastrophic conflict is "inevitable."

| | | | | [|
---](https://roseforcongress.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=35bf91c695e8f4a5dc8a9dd42&id=2fd153db29&e=8c53948e4c)
| | | | | |
## Say NO to war with Iran
---
| | Friend,
An all too familiar assumption has overtaken Washington, DC. Tensions with Iran continue to rise and we are being told that another conflict is "inevitable."
**But we say NO.**
We refuse to accept a future defined by endless escalation. For decades, the "bipartisan consensus" has treated the American taxpayer like an open checkbook for war and the military-industrial complex. In 2026, we will likely witness a staggering milestone: **a $1 trillion defense budget**.
Meanwhile, our communities are sinking, and necessities are becoming more difficult to afford. We are told there is "no money" for the things people really want, like **healthcare, education, and affordable housing.** But still, our government threatens to start yet another costly and destructive war in the Middle East. And working people will remain stuck hoping a surprise medical bill doesn’t send them into bankruptcy.
**That’s why we must stand together in saying NO to war with Iran.**
[**Will you stand with us to reject war with Iran and demand a budget that puts people over war profiteering? Every dollar helps us move our campaign forward.**](https://roseforcongress.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=35bf91c695e8f4a5dc8a9dd42&id=17c191b545&e=8c53948e4c)
Every dollar spent on war is a dollar that isn’t going to your healthcare, education, or helping to lower the costs of child care or buying a home. Instead they pay for "forever wars" and overseas bases that do nothing to make the average American safer.
**We have a choice: we can continue to be an empire abroad and a failing state at home, or we can bring our tax dollars back to work for us.**
[**Can you spare a few dollars to help bring my campaign’s vision for peace and cooperation to Washington, D.C.?**](https://roseforcongress.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=35bf91c695e8f4a5dc8a9dd42&id=972cb76ea8&e=8c53948e4c)
Together, let’s choose a future where people, peace, and planet are at the center of our policies, not war and profit.
---
| |

In solidarity,Rose Penelope YeeCandidate, US Congress CA-02

subject: This is unamerican
body:
Peter,
I wanted to emphasize just how serious of a moment we are in.
Donald Trump’s federal agents are going door to door in Minnesota looking for folks based on their accent or color of their skin. Kids are afraid to go to school, small businesses are hurting, another life has been lost, and the people responsible have yet to be held accountable. Instead, Donald Trump’s DOJ is investigating me.
Why? Because my focus has always been protecting the people of Minnesota.
They’re trying to scare me and our state — but Minnesota will not be intimidated into silence and neither will I. This legal battle will be expensive, that’s why they’re doing this. They want me to back down and surrender, but I won’t.
I need your help in this fight. If you’re able, please split a donation between our Legal Defense fund and Outrage then Action PAC and make sure we can continue to stand up to Donald Trump and his DOJ? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp_2026_dga?refcode=partner_ms_tw_em_022026_realtexaspac]

Friends,
I just left a room that felt like a living civic nerve center--where community care, moral authority, and institutional power were all present at once, and (for a few minutes) aligned.
It was the **Compassion in Action Iftar Reception** , hosted by the **Somali Family Safety Task Force** and the **Washington African Diaspora Commission** --an invitation-only gathering built around a deceptively simple idea: we don't just break our fast together. We build civic bonds together. We honor leadership and belonging, and we do it in a way that's rooted in dignity, respect, and shared responsibility.
If you've never been to an iftar like this, here's what you should know: a well-held Ramadan gathering is not "just an event." It's a kind of social architecture. It's where grief and gratitude sit side by side. It's where people who rarely share a table--across faith, across class, across role--suddenly do. And in that shift, you can feel something reassemble in the public life of a city.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7a7f9d4c-163c-4082-806a-0cf150cce03d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The room**
This crowd was high-density in the way only certain rooms are:
* \- The Mayor of Seattle, Katie Wilson, plus at least four members of her executive team
* \- Mayors and city councilmembers from four other cities
* \- Erika Adams, the new Seattle City Attorney
* \- Civil rights leaders, nonprofit leadership, faith leaders, community elders, organizers, and advocates from across the region

I'm naming that not to "name-drop," but because we don't always tell the truth about how change moves. It moves through policy, yes. It moves through budgets, yes. But it also moves through relationships, through cultural legitimacy, through who is trusted enough to speak and who is trusted enough to be heard.
In other words: some moments are worth noticing because they're leverage points. This was one of them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d8866f9c-3280-4e2d-9700-cae5ee78f1f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**A declaration that made history**
The Mayor made a declaration that landed: she dedicated today, February 27, 2026 to the African Diaspora communities of Washington State.
That is not nothing.
Words can be cheap, and I do not worship symbolism. But I also don't dismiss it--because symbolism is part of how institutions communicate who belongs, who is seen, and whose safety and dignity are part of the "we."
And for Ahmed Mumin--a friend, and the initiator of this gathering, and the founder of the Washington African Diaspora Commission--it was a meaningful public acknowledgment of what he and many others have been building: not just services, not just events, but a durable civic presence.
**The human logistics behind "public life"**
Let me bring this down to earth for a moment, because I want to honor the reality that sits behind the polished photos and formal remarks.
I went into this evening not in some glamorous stride of effortless readiness--but as a tired human who needed help getting there.
My mom drove. I napped in the car. I still have the hospital wristband on as I type this. Mom was kind enough to have loperamide in her purse--because life is sometimes very literal and not at all aesthetic.
This is part of the truth of leadership too: you show up when maybe you should go home and sleep. You show up anyway, carrying your body, your nervous system, your family logistics, your vulnerabilities, your invisible costs. And then you step into the room and do the work anyway.
So when we talk about "community leaders," I want us to also remember the quiet infrastructure behind the scenes--the people who make our showing-up possible.
**I spoke after the Mayor**
And then: I got called up to speak after the Mayor of Seattle.
If you've ever done public speaking, you know the feeling. The room is warm, full, attentive--and the stakes are higher than they look. You have minutes, not hours. You don't get a do-over. **You can either rise to the moment, or you can shrink inside your own self-consciousness.**
We choose to rise to those moments because we believe in something bigger than ourselves. Because the message matters more than our limitations. For me, this was a moment to do what I care about most--bring something true into the room.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99a6c28d-f811-491a-8bb7-b6d433ce095f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**And personally --having Zahid there mattered.**
There are moments when "public life" can feel abstract: podiums, titles, agendas, the practiced choreography of who speaks when. But this evening was also deeply, unmistakably human. My husband, Zahid, was there beside me--home after four months of wrongful detention by ICE--standing in the same room as the Mayor of Seattle, her executive team, city leaders, and community elders. Watching him move through that space with steadiness and dignity felt like witnessing a door reopen in real time: not just a return to community, but a return to belonging.
He spoke from the stage about courage, community, and integrity--and specifically about what it means to stay anchored when pressure comes to trade your conscience for personal safety or gain. He reminded the room that Ramadan strips life down to what is essential: we are not what we accumulate, but what we remember and what we give. He named his family's refugee lineage--India to Pakistan--carrying "nothing in their hands, but everything in their hearts," and he connected that inheritance to the oath he took in uniform to defend the Constitution.
Then he said something I keep turning over: "Sabr is not passive. Patience is not silence. Steadfastness is a form of service." That line landed like a bell. Because it's true in faith, and it's true in civic life. In a time when so many people are being pushed--quietly or overtly--to betray their principles to survive, Zahid offered a different template: hold the line, stay present to one another, and remember the table is wide enough.
For me, it wasn't just moving. It was clarifying. This is what integrity looks like when it has a body. This is what community means when it refuses to abandon its own. And I left grateful--not only for the honor of speaking--but for the simple fact that we were there together.
**Mercy as Method**
I spoke from a framework I'm developing in my forthcoming book, **Mercy as Method** : the idea that Islam does not only offer private virtue, but public guidance--a structure for leadership, for restraint, for accountability, for human dignity as a baseline rather than a reward.
In Ramadan, we don't fast to suffer. We fast to recalibrate. We're training ourselves to choose restraint when we could indulge, patience when we could react, generosity when we could hoard.
And that isn't just spiritual practice. It's leadership training.
Because the people entrusted with power--whether in government, institutions, nonprofits, or community structures--are constantly confronted with choices that test the soul:
* \- Will you treat people as problems to manage, or as humans to honor?
* \- Will you make "efficiency" your god, or will you protect dignity as the non-negotiable baseline?
* \- Will you punish in ways that satisfy anger, or hold accountability in ways that reduce future harm?

One line I included in the talk is one I want to lodge into the public imagination:
**" The purpose of power is to ensure those who have none still lead lives of dignity, safety, and opportunity."**
That line isn't partisan. It's moral. It's universal. It's the measure by which any society can judge the integrity of its institutions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0be7551-a82e-4142-8d30-9a68c7adbdbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The point of an iftar like this**
Events like this are not "nice." They are not ornamental. They are part of how we repair the social fabric--especially at a time when the public sphere is being flooded with fear, coercion, and cynicism.
An iftar is an act of public trust-building. And this one carried a quiet message that mattered:
Washington's African Muslim immigrant communities are not "on the margins." They are central. They are builders. They are civic leadership. They are part of the moral center of the region.
And the leaders who show up--mayors, attorneys, executives, organizers--are making a choice about what kind of city and state we become.
**A personal aftertaste**
I left feeling grateful. And also clear-eyed.
Moments like these are rare: where community legitimacy and institutional power occupy the same space, and where you can feel real possibility in the air--possibility rooted not in slogans, but in relationships and shared moral language.
It was worth it. Entirely.
Not because it felt good (though it did). But because in a time when so much public life is flattened into performance, this felt like something else: a table where people remembered what leadership is for.
May we build more tables like this.
Ramadan Mubarak.
-- Melissa

name: Tom Fitton
subject: Update on Minneapolis Daycare Centers!
body:
NY City: Millions on Migrants

[INSIDE JW]

RECORDS SHOW RAMPANT VIOLATIONS IN MINNEAPOLIS DAYCARE CENTERS

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37243&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS9rUUZMcC1qUzQ5Yz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=1a3791149c58ab285eeb2a8d98be3e767561b69db4c648bda92d6f50356be771]

We received 458 pages
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37209&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=3545c63e543dc443809137cfb0491c59e761f60c6eef4a3a4747a833d27ee93a] of
records from the Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
in a Minnesota Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request that show a
strong pattern of false billing, misstated attendance records,
repeated licensing violations, grant fraud, and inadequate supervision
of children across multiple daycare facilities in Minneapolis.

The number of violations and intentionally false reporting committed
by these facilities is staggering.

We obtained the records in response to our December 2025 state FOIA
request. They show that the Minnesota Department of Human Services
conducted video surveillance comparisons, attendance record audits,
and financial grant audits that identified fraudulent billing at
multiple facilities with overpayments totaling hundreds of thousands
of dollars assessed, and in some cases, facilities continuing to
operate and accrue new violations even after prior enforcement
actions.

In August 2019, the Minnesota Department of Human Services issued a
Correction Order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37210&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjA0LTIxNC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=cd0f8f9f33a479de34b7527b3a7473abec27c5f778646e4dc67413010f72e3b4]
to the Minnesota Child Care Center, citing staff qualification
deficiencies: four staff persons did not have documentation on site
showing they met the education and experience requirements for their
teacher job classifications. The order states “This is a repeat
licensing violation. The license holder was cited for a similar
violation in a Correction Order dated April 25, 2017.”

Human Services in September 2019, ordered
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37211&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjE1LTIxOC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=5ce40fed6546088d31498719cfc8cfad04f39e23d2d1af8ed6f79dcc77ab0a8f]
the Minnesota Child Care Center to pay a fine. The order states:
“The Department of Human Services (DHS) is ordering you to pay a
fine of $600 for three background study violations.... [Y]ou failed to
request background studies for three staff persons before they began
working in positions allowing direct contact with children served by
your program.”

Human Services issued an Administrative Disqualification and Notice of
Refusal to Pay
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37212&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMS03Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=b4549dae2af0a44afc498b4d3f9897d4d19dc03afd8641c1f634513affa2025c]
against Minnesota Child Care Center in August 2022, finding the center
“intentionally gave materially false information on billing forms
and/or provided false attendance records.” State Child Care
Assistance Program payments were immediately stopped, all
authorizations were closed, and the facility and its principals were
disqualified from receiving Child Care Assistance Program payments for
three years.

A Department of Human Services investigation found significant
discrepancies between video footage of children entering the building
and its attendance records. In numerous 15-minute intervals across
late 2018, attendance records showed children arriving when no
children were observed on video.

The review also found that from 2018 through 2021, the center billed
for multiple holidays that did not meet Child Care Assistance Program
payment criteria, often claiming both holiday pay and regular
attendance on the same day.

Analysis of six billing periods (November 19, 2018, through February
10, 2019) found that “361 of the 4,711 dates of [Child Care
Assistance Program] billing reviewed, attendance records did not meet
record keeping requirements” — including 187 missing sign-in
times, 262 missing sign-out times, and 14 missing records entirely.

The center was informed:

What is the effect of being disqualified?

> In addition to being disqualified from accepting [Child Care
> Assistance Program] payments for three years, a disqualification may
> also affect your ability to clear a background study, hold a child
> care license or certification, have direct contact or access to
> children in a child care setting, and/or participate in other
> Department of Human Services programs.

***

> In addition, because of the [Child Care Assistance Program]
> violations, we estimate Minnesota Child Care Center Inc. was
> overpaid $24,480.38.

On August 22, 2022, a Notice of Overpayment
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37213&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtOC05Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=d68a5003e742000aa86d5a0038acac7cc410651a864e8ba8d3aeadf91166b04e]
was issued against Minnesota Child Care Center regarding the
$24,480.38.

In October 2023, Minnesota Child Care Center was ordered to pay a fine
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37214&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjMwLTIzMy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=e472b9ecf5185d60a01c93b47075f5e31fb9922bffb5aa21fe5240aa63d341e4].
The order states: “The Department of Human Services (DHS) is
ordering you to pay a fine of $1200 for six background study
violations.” The six violations involved staff who had been working
in direct contact positions without federally required enhanced
background studies.

In April 2024, Human Services determined that Minnesota Child Care
Center failed to complete a carpet replacement project for which it
received a $9,990.40 Facility Revitalization Grant in June 2022. The
facility received a 90% disbursement of $8,991.36 but failed to submit
the required final report with before/after photos and expense
documentation by the November 30, 2022, deadline. The Notice of
Overpayment
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37215&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjMtMjUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=5ba883cf74b579a40281d027e4fc361706e95a8e78cd7ed46172597b99198e9f]
states:

> You did not meet the requirements of the Facility Revitalization
> Grant for the March 2022 grant period as you failed to submit
> required project completion information and documentation by
> November 30, 2022. You will need to reimburse DHS for the recovery
> of the awarded grant money, totaling $8,991.36, for this grant
> period.

The Minnesota Child Care Center was issued a Correction Order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37216&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjQxLTI0OC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=3de893c2013a5c4ce3a24a4b38ae21255af80f7a892d017e03a3fdd0fb097f7c]
in October 2024 that cited several violations. The order noted that
this was a repeat offense
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37217&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjM0LTI0MC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=f125fe6357a25a1c00d09cd816119bb0f8ab6c703edcb66dde28b8d53e6e78e4]
that included:

> Violation: Staff distribution requirements were not maintained. A
> teacher or assistant teacher did not directly supervise an aide.

> An aide was working alone with three infant-aged children. A staff
> person with the qualifications of a teacher was required....

> Two aide qualified individuals were alone with twelve school-aged
> children. A staff person with the qualifications of a teacher was
> required....

> Repeat Licensing Violation: The license holder was cited for a
> similar violation in the following order(s): A Correction Order
> dated October 31, 2023.

In November 2024, Minnesota Child Care Center was ordered to pay a
fine
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37218&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjQ5LTI1My8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=1259d21fb9acd2fb6ba9c3953dc853e32978eaff2944490dab4a4fd6808a08b9].
The order states: “The Department of Human Services (DHS) is
ordering you to pay a fine of $1600 for eight background study
violations.”

Among the eight violations, one staff person (SP1) had a background
study that expired December 31, 2022. After being ordered to remove
SP1 in October 2023, the facility initiated a background study but
failed to submit fingerprints within 14 days, causing the study to
lapse. SP1 continued working at the center and was still present when
Human Services returned in October 2024.

In October 2025, the state issued a separate Notice of Overpayment
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37219&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMzEtMzIvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=ac2367a798ddcb99946680444d7c0b69f0fed6170ecc27a3167f16b9cf83a86e]
against Minnesota Child Care Center for $9,408 for billing
irregularities during December 9, 2024, to January 5, 2025 — more
than two years after the facility was disqualified from the program.

In December 2025, Minnesota Child Care Center was ordered
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37220&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjU5LTI2Mi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=743abaa4ad656650a336ca1c5a912e37a99c639cfbdd21c434917941c7801337]
“to pay a $200 fine for one background study violation.” The order
documented a staff person (SP1), who had been employed since August
2001 and whose background study was repeatedly mishandled. An enhanced
study was initiated in October 2023, but fingerprints were not
submitted within 14 days, causing it to lapse. A second attempt was
initiated in October 2024, but the same fingerprint submission failure
occurred again. The facility had been informed three times in 2022
that enhanced studies were federally required.

In August 2022, Human Services disqualified
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37221&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMTAtMTUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=7f5411b7203975483f0f5f5004fc0facaf61a6e8d095eb4b3cc50e2b00a8f739]
Nuna Child Care Center (which shared the same address as Minnesota
Child Care Center) from the Child Care Assistance Program after
investigators found “materially false information on billing forms
and/or provided false attendance records.”

Human Services cited numerous discrepancies between surveillance video
of children entering the 312 W. Lake St. building and the center’s
attendance records, with many instances where children were reported
as arriving but were not observed on video. A review of six billing
periods from November 2018 through February 2019 found:

> For 1,250 of the 2,055 dates of [Child Care Assistance Program]
> billings reviewed, attendance records did not meet record keeping
> requirements for one or more of the following reasons:

* In 18 instances, no attendance record was provided;
* In 1,144 instances, the attendance record were missing a time in;
* In 1,187 instances, attendance records were missing a time out;

* Billing Record Does Not Match Attendance Record: 16

* In 16 instances, children were billed in attendance (Regular), but
attendance records show the children marked absent or vice versa.

Human Services also found improper holiday billing.

A Notice of Overpayment
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37222&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMTYtMTcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=7ca5f6b159ba112e2fbeeffd858a590391a26d9b23bd311111d7d4bd4987bdc2]
for $72,529.85 was issued against Nuna Child Care Center on August 22,
2022, for the period of November 19, 2018, through February 10, 2019.

In December 2024, Nuna Childcare Center was issued a Correction Order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37223&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjc4LTI4Mi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=afcdf7de431fcc81e46f580ec5c1e24f206070216569196d62516daf07ed0df4],
documenting multiple supervision failures within a single afternoon
visit. The order states:

> Violation: Staff did not supervise the children at all times (School
> Age).

* At approximately 4:41 p.m., a child ran from the preschool
classroom to the school age classroom alone....
* At approximately 5:05 p.m., a child ran from the preschool
classroom to the school age classroom alone....
* At approximately 5:17 p.m., a teacher left three children alone in
the classroom to grab something out of the lobby....

Three separate unsupervised-child incidents were observed within 36
minutes. This order was issued more than two years after Nuna’s 2022
Child Care Assistance Program disqualification, demonstrating
continued operational deficiencies at the facility.

In April 2023, the state issued a Notice of Overpayment
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37224&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjEtMjIvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=f6dc550a0f20d95c6b2b3593158a447dc52481a1b10ec102c43fd48c76beb7e3]
for $47,487.80 against Mini Childcare Center for the period of
November 28, 2022, through December 25, 2022. The notice states:

* In 709 instances, you failed to make attendance records available
upon request.
* In 26 instances, you failed to document the time a child was signed
out of care.
* In 27 instances, you submitted billing for children that indicated
they were absent, when records indicate the children were actually
present and receiving care.

Human Services issued a Notice of Overpayment
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37225&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtMjYtMjkvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=ccb712b64b96c07b53e07981d207ab0f84a9f408f17aa74fcb4f1e5e9e872b4e]
in July 2024 for $76,000 against ABC Learning Center for four
Financial Hardship Grants in 2022. The center was informed it failed
to “meet the requirements of the Financial Hardship Grants ... as
the financial records did not reflect your claims on the Financial
Hardship Grant applications. You will need to reimburse [Human
Services] for the recovery of the awarded grant money ...”

In November 2025, a Correction Order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79919&L=37226&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21uLWRheWNhcmUtZnJhdWQtMjAyNi1wZ3MtNTItNTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=2353609533dd01e671c7f29a12581a41e6a59acba4f3c8ef95a7988b7f3e2420]
was issued against ABC Learning Center after inspectors observed
children left without supervision. The order states:

> At approximately 3:12 p.m., the [Dept of Children, Youth and
> Families] licensors observed seven school aged children unsupervised
> in the school age classroom while a staff person walked down to the
> toddler and preschool classroom.

Additional violations included menus that did not comply with U.S.
