_[Note: I wrote this post before Trump & Netanyahu's illegal strikes on Iran, which I will address in a separate post in the coming days.]_
Earlier this week, the president delivered the annual State of the Union address to Congress. The longest such address in the history of the Republic, it may have also been the least thoughtful or credible.
Buried within the president's speech, however, was a crucial reflection on corruption that--along with the Democratic Party's official response to it--revealed how deeply the rot within America has festered.
The next time you hear either a Republican or Democrat talk about corruption, remind them that their own party leaders are up to their necks in it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b1d78f60-442c-4a81-893a-73f426621ba7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **Observing civil liberties in exile**
I was recently invited by Flashpoints Radio, a nationally syndicated program on the Pacifica Network, to reflect on a series of constitutional issues. Our most recent discussion focused on Trump's State of the Union address on Tuesday night, but might not be archived online yet.
Before digging into the analysis I shared with Flashpoints during our interview on Wednesday, I figured I'd share [our interview from January 28](https://substack.com/redirect/f458345d-ca31-4cac-b815-5b88399d51d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reflecting on civil liberties, and efforts by the states to resist the authoritarianism promoted by the federal government. My appearance begins at 46:20, and includes reflections on the [ICE murders of Renee Good and Alex Pretti](https://substack.com/redirect/e8bb25cd-93cd-427b-8eb6-74cbf1112e7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Minneapolis.

### **Convenient reflections on corruption**
This week's [State of the Union address](https://substack.com/redirect/e8bb25cd-93cd-427b-8eb6-74cbf1112e7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) rambled across a wide variety of themes, but one in particular struck me as especially revealing: corruption. Predictably ignoring how his administration has been seemingly focused on filling his pockets, the president instead drew attention to other, more convenient, examples:
> Let's also ensure that members of Congress cannot corruptly profit from using insider information. They stood up for that. I can't believe it. I can't believe it. Did Nancy Pelosi stand up, if she's here? Doubt it. Pass the Stop Insider Trading Act without delay. I wasn't sure if anybody even on this side was going to applaud for that. I'm very impressed. Thank you. I'm very impressed.
> ...
> This is the kind of corruption that shreds the fabric of a nation, and we are working on it....
Having run for Congress against the literal poster child of congressional corruption, only to be publicly silenced by an [Islamophobic character assassination](https://substack.com/redirect/225ded8a-35d3-495f-b95e-3358dfa6a08f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) orchestrated across her political party to insulate her so-called "leadership," it felt jarring to hear an unrepentant autocrat single out the brand of self-enrichment through public office with which the name [Pelosi has become synonymous](https://substack.com/redirect/d7b0d35a-051f-4df5-8749-46a4d662eeea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
_Chronicles of a Dying Empire is a publication made possible by readers, rather than advertisers. To receive new posts,**sign up for a free subscription**! To support my work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber._
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..ZNVo0r7TtgQILn5OZpCcVZwsZr5BzwvYRZ5UMjjXVt4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=189434750)
Trump took advantage of an attack surface created by the corruption among Democrats who remain committed to insider trading and the constitutional violations inherent in it. This issue is the key to why Trump remains in office, and was not impeached back in 2020 when he could have been removed had Pelosi not [slow-walked impeachment](https://substack.com/redirect/3737fefe-0b01-4f21-9d11-19cb74d84e90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and then shown up like a boxer throwing a fight.
To respond to Trump, the Democratic Party chose a CIA agent who currently serves as the Governor of Virginia, Abigail Spanberger. She [observed](https://substack.com/redirect/c656da1b-14c6-4842-b248-670eae19c099?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), among other things, the president's remarkably shameless hypocrisy:
> Is the president working for you? We all know the answer is no. Who benefits from his rhetoric, his policies, his actions, the short list of laws he's pushed through this Republican Congress?
> Somebody must be benefiting. He's enriching himself, his family, his friends. The scale of the corruption is unprecedented.
Aside from the obvious corruption implicit in letting an intelligence agent govern a major state, or serve as the Democratic Party's [national mouthpiece](https://substack.com/redirect/95e0dce8-107e-40c2-99fa-72eaf7397805?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the sheer audacity of Spanberger reflecting on the president's self-enrichment--without observing the [tragically bipartisan](https://substack.com/redirect/5ed4fb58-2494-4fce-ab83-e3819604cf3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nature of the problem--felt breathtaking.
An entire country is watching plutocrats fight over which among them gets to fleece the American people to fund their lavish lifestyles.
Whether it's Trump steering federal dollars into his bank account, or Pelosi [using inside information](https://substack.com/redirect/adbc5130-f0a1-4ae1-89d0-e6e8a438af13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to trade stocks, it's all unconstitutional--yet not illegal, since Congress writes the laws, exempted its members from the same rules to which the rest of us remain subject, and affirmatively refused to allow the constitutional Emoluments Clause to be a subject of the 2020 impeachment proceedings.
The Constitution's Emoluments Clause was written with a single purpose in mind: to prevent officials from enriching themselves through public office. As [I wrote at a moment in time before](https://substack.com/redirect/d853bf8c-58be-4644-a8e0-14f3b653b7ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Pelosi was finally forced to proceed with impeachment, that clause should have been at the heart of the 2020 impeachment proceedings--but when Pelosi did finally allow impeachment to proceed, she affirmatively limited the process to protect the class interests that she and Trump share.
The next time you hear either a Republican or Democrat talk about corruption, remind them that their own party leaders are up to their necks in it.

### **No, the Supreme Court is not coming to save us**
Last week, the Supreme Court [struck down](https://substack.com/redirect/0cce4d56-bc61-4d72-b527-e0217f7c31ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Trump's signature tariffs. It was the first time the Court has intervened to block any of Trump's second term policies, and featured a [surprising cast](https://substack.com/redirect/a9c6981d-14af-4715-be2d-d5e096dff4f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of characters, with three of the Court's reliably conservative votes--Roberts, Barrett, and Gorsuch--joining the three Justices who more consistently vote against them (Kagan, Sotomayor, and Jackson).
Many observers wrote in the wake of the decision about the [possibility](https://substack.com/redirect/6d7f22fc-3ed1-4751-b7b5-d1fe867eabf1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the Court rediscovering its independence, and the possibility of more assertive checks & balances coming from a branch of the government that has generally deferred to Trump's authoritarianism.
But the decision striking down the president's arbitrary tariffs in no way represents the Court flexing its independence.
First, it's not clear whether the decision will even make a difference in policy. True to form, the president immediately castigated the Justices, heaping [ad hominem scorn](https://substack.com/redirect/53e5299f-aae6-42cd-be84-508c9eb5ff6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) upon even those who he himself appointed. Equally [true to form](https://substack.com/redirect/f67c7416-4b16-4913-86ab-2eb540173feb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), he also circumvented the Court, by [reviving his tariffs](https://substack.com/redirect/eeb01394-7144-4edd-8f31-85505f57cf30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) under a different purported legal authority.
Second, the rare alignment that brought Roberts, Barrett, and Gorsuch together with Kagan, Jackson, and Sotomayor is a reflection not of judicial independence, so much as judicial servitude to Wall Street.
Kagan, Jackson, and Sotomayor were likely motivated by their constitutional role of checking & balancing the president. They often attempt to do that by casting votes in the Court's relatively consistent minority. The Roberts-Barrett-Gorsuch block, however, was likely more motivated by their allegiance to Wall Street. Every one of those Justices came to the Court after demonstrating their fealty to capital for decades.
American businesses have been rightfully critical of the president's tariff schemes since they were first announced. [Markets initially responded](https://substack.com/redirect/14dfde08-bd80-4f11-b8ad-14043273db00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Court's ruling positively, before realizing the [uncertainty left in its wake](https://substack.com/redirect/ae4fbd33-dc50-4491-952f-ffe671efe129?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Markets are notoriously fickle, so there's no reason to expect coherence in either their response, or the jurisprudence contrived by Justices inclined to serve their whims.
But the idea that the Court is back in the business of defending the Constitution is simply absurd. The tariffs decision simply reflects some of the right wing Justices prioritizing their longstanding patron--Wall Street--above the particular president who appointed them.
He'll eventually go the way of all living beings. But the markets, and the Justices' allegiance to them, will remain.

### **Another switch in time?**
Eighty-nine years ago, a different Supreme Court Justice took a position that [surprised](https://substack.com/redirect/20bbe767-c291-4f1b-b207-fca077b6820b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) onlookers. When Justice Owen Roberts filed his opinion in _[West Coast Hotel v. Parrish](https://substack.com/redirect/40113f72-3dc0-49cf-8cb1-8aacde33cce9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , he effectively conceded a point over which the Supreme Court had repeatedly tussled with then President Franklin D. Roosevelt.
In particular, Roosevelt had sought to pass various laws to protect working class Americans from the vagaries of the Great Depression, only to be stymied by a Court hellbent on enforcing economic laissez faire policies as a constitutional principle.
Lacking any textual basis, their commitment to blocking economic regulation fell in the face of Roosevelt's intimidation. Threatening to pack the Court by expanding it, Roosevelt effectively invited the Justices to either get on board with the needs of the country, or instead find themselves resigned to individual insignificance.
Justice Roberts (Owen, not John) saw the writing on the wall, conceded to Roosevelt, and helped decide the case that launched the New Deal. It came to be known as "[The switch in time that saved nine](https://substack.com/redirect/20bbe767-c291-4f1b-b207-fca077b6820b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
This year's tariff's case might ultimately come to represent a part in a similar saga, nearly a century later.
On Tuesday night, Trump mentioned the tariffs ruling in his State of the Union address. He described it as "unfortunate" (twice) while three of the Justices who ruled against him were present.
Unlike his statements in the immediate wake of their ruling, however, Trump on Tuesday neither named the Justices, nor berated them, nor described them as "a [disgrace](https://substack.com/redirect/6b41e79b-50d3-4ce0-8e18-6bb8200a814c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to our nation," or "[disloyal](https://substack.com/redirect/a69929b3-e9e5-452a-baac-a1bcf7ec4b72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to our Constitution."
Could the amelioration of his rhetoric on Tuesday represent an attempt to ingratiate himself to the same Justices who he dragged in public only a few days earlier? Even though the right wing split reflected the primary allegiance of some Justices to Wall Street, Trump's earlier ad hominem attacks could have inspired greater potential judicial independence going forward--but his conciliatory tone towards them on Tuesday looked like an attempt to recover their allegiance.
Only time will tell how this standoff between the president and the Supreme Court will resolve itself. In the meantime, don't hold your breath imagining that the Justices will finally begin defending civil liberties. Too many overlook [the role they have played](https://substack.com/redirect/d213c4c5-157c-4b68-bd14-fc9f1d277e6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over the past generation.

### **A canary 's mind (1/18/26)**
What does a canary feel
as it watches a miner
dig ever deeper
even as it offers
its very last breath
in warning?
Does the canary think
of people stabbing
in the neck all of their heirs
their ignorance comfortably
striking out from behind
a veil of intergenerational
anonymity?
Does the canary wonder
what works of art and science
will be lost to the coming crisis?
As the engines of supposed
civilization finally array themselves
against it?
Might the canary think
"So sad to see them go!
Their bald heads made
good targets?"
Will canaries mourn
that no one will build more
statues on which to leave
behind a trail of
their passing?
Do they know
if they came from dinosaurs
what will eventually
become of us?
or does it simply think
"Damn fools, I tried
to warn you?"
Is THAT
what canaries
are singing?
With my last
dying breath
and every ember
of my being:
"Get the fuck out
of here now,
before it's too late!"
Will it remember
in the next life?
What does a canary feel
while singing?
If only, freed
from the mine
and burden of being
a messenger
it enjoyed one
more chance to fly
among conifers
drinking in
the magenta
and fuchsia tones
of a neon sunset

Midnight tonight. That's our deadline.
When the clock strikes 12, our February fundraising window closes. And here's what happens next: We finalize our March budget based on what we raised. Digital ads. Door knockers. Campaign literature. Organizing infrastructure across the district.
Hit our goal? We execute our full plan and compete at the level we need to win.
Fall short? We have to scale back and make tough choices about what we can afford.
I'm Mel Tull. I'm a veteran, a business lawyer, and a community leader running to flip one of the most competitive congressional districts in Virginia. Redistricting gave us a real shot. Democrats have momentum across the country. We have everything we need to win this race.
Except one thing: We need to hit our February goal tonight.
This isn't abstract. These numbers determine our March budget. Whether we can run digital ads introducing me to voters. Whether we can hire canvassers to knock doors across the district. Whether we can print literature and build the organizing infrastructure to flip this seat.
We set an ambitious goal: $5,500 by midnight tonight. Right now, we're close — but we're not there yet.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Today, Marilyn gives you an inside look into what it was like for her growing up in Mexican Narco Territory after her once peaceful area was taken by Narco expansion.
Many Mexicans[ believe that the US could play a role in countering narco-terrorism](https://substack.com/redirect/7b88606e-a100-4cc3-8c16-bd18c4dd29f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). After all, narco-terrorist organizations wouldn't exist without massive US drug demand and an equally large flow of money and weapons back into Mexico--often supported by corporate and financial structures located in the US. But as much as many can imagine a path for cooperation, there is a lot of uncertainty, fear, and distrust in the US's ability to do it right. _****_
Now, Marilyn recounts the sadness and fear she encountered living among terrorists, and potential paths forward. -Lucas

This past Sunday, news outlets once again turned their eyes to Mexico. [Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera Cervantes](https://substack.com/redirect/cab830e0-8f72-40b0-9f3a-fa64be9d09bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the elusive leader of the [Jalisco New Generation Cartel](https://substack.com/redirect/355a7c52-effc-4fad-9b90-3269262df5b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (CJNG), [was killed in a military operation](https://substack.com/redirect/59e4af6a-0c85-4eeb-ac25-da72613d747c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) carried out by Mexican security forces with U.S. intelligence support. He led a criminal enterprise with tentacles throughout Mexican territory and into [all 50 ](https://substack.com/redirect/129374b4-9e51-4a47-a3e6-574f5cd075ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)US States and over 40 countries.
Headlines like this about Mexico today might not be shocking, but to me, that wasn't always the case. I have talked before about growing up in Mexico _**.**_ In those days, Mexico felt wide, safe, and unguarded.
My earliest memories are of long highway rides, where the biggest threat was a coyote darting into the road or the rare encounter with a drunk driver. My parents talking in the front seat, the stereo playing my mom's favorite songs, the landscape rolling out peacefully before us. We roamed freely in the back of our purple 1991 Ford E-150 van.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6be8480a-8434-4468-854d-ca4b104f5b59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Little Marilyn beside her family 's purple Ford van in the driveway of their home in Guadalupe Victoria, Durango, Mexico_
In our corner of Mexico, like most of the country, there was no such thing as a "narco culture." No sense that violence could interrupt on an ordinary Tuesday.
Then, in 2010, in my senior year of high school, the ground shifted.
That year we were supposed to take a school trip to some touristic part of the country. It was a rite of passage at our school, permission to see more of our own country that was vast, beautiful, and ours to discover without fear. My sister had gone to Puerto Vallarta on hers. My brother walked among pyramids and ancient ruins on his. Now it was finally my turn!
I wondered whether I would finally make it to a beach washed in gold light, I imagined stepping onto warm sand for the first time. My friends and I speculated endlessly at every break we had between classes.
But it never happened.
What had once been routine became unthinkable almost overnight.
That year, everything changed for us back in my hometown, and stories of carefree school trips became a distant memory.
We learned what it meant to shelter in place, not for a storm, but for men with rifles. We spent days inside while what sounded like a war zone unfolded outside our windows. [Streets emptied into ghost towns](https://substack.com/redirect/5be1e4e0-339e-4128-b5ea-68ccb29870ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Schools closed. [Businesses shuttered](https://substack.com/redirect/2cc67d98-f83c-44bf-bf6d-5689ecbe60c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Government offices locked their doors.
2010 brought a darkness we had never known in my hometown, nor in so many corners of Mexico. [Town officials were killed](https://substack.com/redirect/d0e46680-162e-4ce8-a252-7cf81dcf2e05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in front of their families. Police officers were assassinated or resigned because resisting was futile. The cartels did not merely outnumber them; [they outgunned them](https://substack.com/redirect/ba046293-6085-4829-9819-92952aaa4dfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), wielding weapons and bulletproof glass that most of us had only seen in films and that certainly weren't made in Mexico.
[And then there were the disappearances](https://substack.com/redirect/230a5d22-67ba-4f8f-ad04-725157bdd227?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), boys I grew up with vanished. More than half of the missing and unlocated persons cases were in the age range between 15 and 34 years. We heard whispers that many were coerced into working for the cartels to protect their families, [a pattern unfolding across the country](https://substack.com/redirect/3265ffe8-4c40-4722-b1d7-90d625abecc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In Durango alone, my hometown, [the trend of disappearances that spiked in 2010 is clear](https://substack.com/redirect/230a5d22-67ba-4f8f-ad04-725157bdd227?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0bcc84fc-db1a-4b5b-9f19-ba80f3d77c35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

We did our best to adapt. We learned new routes home. We stopped lingering in the plaza after dark. We lowered our voices when certain names were mentioned. Survival began to masquerade as normalcy.
I will tell you now my own encounter with narcos, and how by fortune alone, I am here to recount it:
In 2011, I moved to Durango City to attend college. I was an 18-year-old freshman and the city felt both thrilling and unfamiliar. I had visited a number of times with my family before, but this was my first time moving around solo.
I had to learn how to navigate buses. A large number of students move around town using the bus system. The routes are long, stretching across neighborhoods and outskirts, and by the time the buses reach the halfway point, there is often no room left for anyone else. The drivers simply pass the remaining stops without slowing down.
My classes began early, the first one of them at 7am. I would plan to catch an earlier bus and if it was too full to stop, I could still take the next one and arrive just on time.
One day, just like any other day, I was at the bus stop waiting for the 6:15am bus, as I had done multiple times now. This was during light saving season, so the morning was still deeply dark.
I saw headlights in the distance from what seemed to be a large vehicle approaching. It could have been a bus, though in that darkness it was hard to tell. I did not think much of it until it passed me.
As it did, a chill ran through my whole body.
I knew exactly who drove vehicles like that in the city. Big trucks were common in rural areas, built for crops and battered roads. But in the city, no one drove those oversized machines without meaning to be seen.
They drive them through town as a statement of dominance.
The only people who drove through Durango City in trucks like that were the cartels.
Another chill ran through me when I saw the vehicle brake, then reverse slowly until it stopped right in front of the only light pole near us. I was the only person there besides them.
I turned as the driver stepped out. A large man, perhaps in his thirties, walked toward me. I could see the gun tucked into his waistband. I tried not to let my eyes linger on it.
Even now I can recall his outline more clearly than his face. The darkness softened his features into fragments. Dark eyes. Dark hair. A broad nose. A poorly trimmed beard. Heavyset. His voice was raspy, words slurred, though not enough to dull his intent.
He smiled.
"What is a young, beautiful lady like yourself doing here all alone? It is dark, you know that, right? It is not safe out here."
I forced a smile in return and steadied my voice. "Yes, I know. I am on my way to college. The bus is just taking a while. But it should be here any minute now."
I wanted him to imagine witnesses arriving, a bus full of students pulling up behind him. I wanted him to feel exposed.
He laughed. I exhaled slowly.
His eyes moved over me, unhurried, enjoying the power of being the one who was not afraid.
He said next, almost casually, "I can give you a ride. My truck is right there. My friend is in it. I am sure he will not mind. In fact, I know he will enjoy your company."
By then my nerves were visible. Running felt useless on that wide, empty road. There was nowhere to hide, nowhere to outrun a bullet. So instead, I turned my back to him.
"No, thanks. I will wait for the bus. It should be here very soon."
I said it as if dismissing a persistent stranger. I hoped he would lose interest.
He did not. And turning your back on a man with a gun is foolish. He drew it and pressed it to my head, grabbing me from behind. I could smell alcohol on his breath as he whispered into my ear, "You are coming with us." He stated.
There was no space for resistance. I walked to the truck and slid into the passenger seat, nodding at whatever they said. The two of them talked about the night before, laughing at memories I could not follow. I barely remember the details. I remember the weapons. One pressed against my side from the back seat. Others lying on the floor.
At some point they mentioned the highway toward Sinaloa. They spoke of a girl already there, waiting. They said she and I would be fun.
My heart pounded so hard. I understood then that release would not come by asking. I studied the roads without turning my head, trying to fix landmarks in my mind. They avoided main avenues, slipping through smaller streets. I wondered whether the man behind me was drunk enough to miss if I ran. His words were still slurred. I decided that if even the smallest chance appeared, I would take it.
Then, a miracle happened.
A car cut in front of us, forcing the truck to stop abruptly. In that same breath, I realized the door beside me was unlocked. I opened it and ran. I did not hesitate. I turned the first corner I saw, then another, slipping through an alley. To my shock, I was not far from campus.
I ran straight to the college building. I did not look back.
Inside, I saw a familiar face and collapsed into sobs.
I had made it.
That morning, a miracle stood between me and becoming another statistic.
**El Mencho**
The man we have all been hearing about in the news, Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera Cervantes was born in rural Michoacan, where boys have long grown up watching [legal agriculture and illicit cultivation co-exist](https://substack.com/redirect/8bcaca5e-82cd-4957-9452-327f626da2c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The line between survival and crime blurred early for them and power was measured in weapons and loyalty. He was [typical of a generation shaped by expanding criminal networks](https://substack.com/redirect/1ff79bbc-11b5-472d-8af2-5b7315d09f2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**,** whose started learning the trade young and whose most direct path to upward mobility was through the cartels--which meant a unique relationship with the United States.
El Mencho immigrated illegally to the US in the 1980s and got his next level of narco-training in the San Francisco Bay Area, . While there he was arrested for weapons and narcotics offenses, served several years in prison, and was deported back to Mexico. While in the US, he became embedded with members of the Valencia crime family, eventually strengthening those ties through marriage. After his return to Mexico, he rose through organized crime ranks and eventually co-founded what became the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG).
He shaped the group into a force [structured like an army](https://substack.com/redirect/16019d8e-c5d2-4666-87a3-0a75e3de873e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and managed like a business.
CJNG became a vertically integrated criminal enterprise: producing and distributing fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine, and heroin; operating clandestine laboratories; acquiring high-powered weapons; stealing and smuggling fuel; extorting businesses and agricultural producers; running timeshare and real estate fraud schemes; engaging in human smuggling and trafficking; expanding into illegal mining; and laundering vast sums through shell companies and cross-border financial networks.
The group earned a reputation as one of the most violent criminal organizations, linked [to tens of thousands of deaths over the past decade](https://substack.com/redirect/7e767f55-6870-4696-afda-49798e157a54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[Rosalinda Gonzalez Valencia](https://substack.com/redirect/23fba9d3-ff47-4b66-b878-561f8b71ee49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), more than simply the spouse of "El Mencho," was widely identified by U.S. and Mexican authorities as a key financial operator within the network tied to the CJNG, and its associated money-laundering structure known as "Los Cuinis".
Rosalinda was alleged to have helped manage a web of businesses across the hospitality, retail, agriculture, and real estate sectors. These companies were [accused by the U.S. Treasury of serving as vehicles to move, disguise, and legitimize cartel proceeds](https://substack.com/redirect/da8ece00-7441-442a-a9b3-cb5fe5ccf709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Gonzalez Valencia was first arrested in 2018 on charges related to illicit financial operations and organized crime, later released on procedural grounds, and then re-arrested. After years of pretrial detention and legal challenges, she was released in 2024, citing insufficient evidence to sustain organized crime charges, although financial investigations had surrounded her case.
Her case highlights [a central tension in dismantling narco enterprises](https://substack.com/redirect/99b2f716-6d7e-4a6b-ac4b-6b3fe44dd64c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): arresting armed leaders is one battle; proving intricate financial conspiracies inside layered corporate structures is another, often far more complicated one.
**The Relationship Between the Cartels and the US**
It is impossible to understand the rise of CJNG without acknowledging the role the United States has played, even if indirectly, in creating the conditions that strengthened it.
**First, there is demand:** [The constant U.S. demand for narcotics, intensified by the opioid crisis and the rapid expansion of fentanyl has proven enormously profitable](https://substack.com/redirect/00949a68-2fe1-47b7-b916-c32e8f64edf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**Second, there is energy supply convenience:**[In Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/6bdeba8e-f9e7-431b-852f-ddafb2e9c122?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), cartel-linked networks have been documented operating near border regions and energy hubs, where stolen crude and fuel are smuggled across the southwest border into the United States and integrated into the legal energy market before eventually being resold and refined.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ae6bc78-f143-48e9-8b52-011d020d5133?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Mexican Cartel Crude Oil Smuggling Schemes. Credit: U.S. Department of the Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control_
This has raised serious questions about why the illegal economy continues to mix with the legal one in Texas, especially [given political rhetoric about border protection](https://substack.com/redirect/f319e7f5-414c-4f73-b78f-13f7822218f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and energy security when these systems remain vulnerable to exploitation by transnational criminal organizations.
**Third, profitable firepower:** [The flow of American weapons is directly linked to increased violence and homicide rates in Mexico](https://substack.com/redirect/a8c74ac0-4c41-4e02-83a0-a321c20c88e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and there is a thriving cross border gun market. Data from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) indicates that [between 70% and 80% of firearms seized in Mexico and submitted for tracing originated north of the border](https://substack.com/redirect/753cb5a3-37f9-4aca-a931-1ae0986cced4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Estimates suggest that over 135,000 firearms are trafficked across the U.S.-Mexico border each year.
**Fourth, revenue streams:** Sophisticated organizations launder funds through legitimate sectors, embedding themselves into legal markets, often in the US, until illicit capital appears ordinary.
If the goal is to meaningfully weaken organizations like CJNG, the strategy cannot rely solely on arrests and military operations, and it certainly can't remain as haphazard as it has been.
When Mexicans think about the US helping solve the problem they have helped create, trust is probably the biggest sticking point. The messages and actions have been so mixed its hard to believe that the US is serious about taking on the problem.
Whether through pardons for individuals convicted of drug related crimes, including the late [2025 pardon of former Honduran president Juan Orlando Hernandez](https://substack.com/redirect/a5382365-bab8-47f2-9302-1cb25454ac82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after his U.S. drug trafficking conviction, or the entering of [17 family members connected to Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman, to the United States](https://substack.com/redirect/353f7f2f-e8d2-4d60-aa36-6b0c5dd7f477?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) through negotiated legal arrangements, the federal government sends conflicting messages about the most basic thing: accountability, which makes it hard to believe that it will be trustworthy about anything.
Protecting Americans, and by extension Mexicans, requires consistency: strong enforcement, transparent standards for clemency and immigration decisions, and financial oversight of corporate infiltration.
**Beyond the Man**
El Mencho's death marked a symbolic milestone. But without addressing the economic and corporate infrastructure that enriched and protected CJNG, its unlikely to be meaningful long term.
The CJNG case illuminates a broader trend: Narco influence is no longer peripheral to the global economy; it is embedded within it.
Policymakers in the United States and around the world, must acknowledge that this cartel already operated, both legally and illegally, across all 50 U.S. states and over 40 countries, and has done so for more than a decade.
That complexity is the sobering truth. The environment that shaped him, the normalization of Narco power as parallel governance, cannot be undone with one operation.
Although the narcos eventually pulled back from my hometown, they did not return to where they began. Instead, they expanded their reach. Their territorial footprint across Mexico is larger now than it was during my childhood, increasing the likelihood that more boys are being socialized within the same violent ecosystems that produced El Mencho.
In order to get real change, we need to rebuild institutions strong enough that we ensure the next boy growing up in a rural town sees a different ladder to climb. The U.S. could, and maybe even should, contribute to that effort give the outsized role it has played in fueling the problem, but only in ways that respect Mexican leadership and sovereignty. I think the biggest barrier to that right now is is that US inconsistency, and perceived double standards, leave Mexicans questioning whether deeper U.S. engagement would be politically viable or even successful within Mexico.
It's a question much of the world seems to be grappling with when thinking about talking to the US right now, and that's a hard truth to accept. In towns like mine, little girls once imagined America as a place that stood for something steady and hopeful. Now it appears less like an exception and more like another potentially bad actor in a complicated, sometimes frightening world.
**Marilyn Kunce**

Gonzalez Valencia was first arrested in 2018 on charges related to illicit financial operations and organized crime, later released on procedural grounds, and then re-arrested. After years of pretrial detention and legal challenges, she was released in 2024, citing insufficient evidence to sustain organized crime charges, although financial investigations had surrounded her case. Her case highlights : arresting armed leaders is one battle; proving intricate financial conspiracies inside layered corporate structures is another, often far more complicated one. The Relationship Between the Cartels and the US It is impossible to understand the rise of CJNG without acknowledging the role the United States has played, even if indirectly, in creating the conditions that strengthened it. First, there is demand: . Second, there is energy supply convenience:, cartel-linked networks have been documented operating near border regions and energy hubs, where stolen crude and fuel are smuggled across the southwest border into the United States and integrated into the legal energy market before eventually being resold and refined. | | ---|---|--- Mexican Cartel Crude Oil Smuggling Schemes. Credit: U.S. Department of the Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control This has raised serious questions about why the illegal economy continues to mix with the legal one in Texas, especially and energy security when these systems remain vulnerable to exploitation by transnational criminal organizations. Third, profitable firepower: , and there is a thriving cross border gun market. Data from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) indicates that . Estimates suggest that over 135,000 firearms are trafficked across the U.S.-Mexico border each year. Fourth, revenue streams: Sophisticated organizations launder funds through legitimate sectors, embedding themselves into legal markets, often in the US, until illicit capital appears ordinary. If the goal is to meaningfully weaken organizations like CJNG, the strategy cannot rely solely on arrests and military operations, and it certainly can't remain as haphazard as it has been. When Mexicans think about the US helping solve the problem they have helped create, trust is probably the biggest sticking point. The messages and actions have been so mixed its hard to believe that the US is serious about taking on the problem. Whether through pardons for individuals convicted of drug related crimes, including the late after his U.S. drug trafficking conviction, or the entering of through negotiated legal arrangements, the federal government sends conflicting messages about the most basic thing: accountability, which makes it hard to believe that it will be trustworthy about anything. Protecting Americans, and by extension Mexicans, requires consistency: strong enforcement, transparent standards for clemency and immigration decisions, and financial oversight of corporate infiltration. Beyond the Man El Mencho's death marked a symbolic milestone. But without addressing the economic and corporate infrastructure that enriched and protected CJNG, its unlikely to be meaningful long term. The CJNG case illuminates a broader trend: Narco influence is no longer peripheral to the global economy; it is embedded within it. Policymakers in the United States and around the world, must acknowledge that this cartel already operated, both legally and illegally, across all 50 U.S. states and over 40 countries, and has done so for more than a decade. That complexity is the sobering truth. The environment that shaped him, the normalization of Narco power as parallel governance, cannot be undone with one operation. Although the narcos eventually pulled back from my hometown, they did not return to where they began. Instead, they expanded their reach. Their territorial footprint across Mexico is larger now than it was during my childhood, increasing the likelihood that more boys are being socialized within the same violent ecosystems that produced El Mencho. In order to get real change, we need to rebuild institutions strong enough that we ensure the next boy growing up in a rural town sees a different ladder to climb. The U.S. could, and maybe even should, contribute to that effort give the outsized role it has played in fueling the problem, but only in ways that respect Mexican leadership and sovereignty. I think the biggest barrier to that right now is is that US inconsistency, and perceived double standards, leave Mexicans questioning whether deeper U.S. engagement would be politically viable or even successful within Mexico. It's a question much of the world seems to be grappling with when thinking about talking to the US right now, and that's a hard truth to accept. In towns like mine, little girls once imagined America as a place that stood for something steady and hopeful. Now it appears less like an exception and more like another potentially bad actor in a complicated, sometimes frightening world. Marilyn Kunce** You're currently a free subscriber to . | | Fellow Patriot,
---
I have to say it...

The campus climate this spring?

_It 's been downright ugly._

To be frank, the Left has never made it easy for our students. That's always come with the territory when you're speaking truth deep in the belly of the beast...

But this semester is different.

**This has been one of the most hostile semesters Turning Point USA students have ever faced. **

From coast to coast, high school and college students who dared to stand for faith, freedom, and this great nation have been stalked, slandered, threatened, and in some cases -- _physically attacked. _

All for saying what you and I know to be true:

That America is worth defending. That speech must remain free. And that Charlie Kirk's life and legacy meant something.

And despite the opposition -- our students didn't back down.

They didn't run. They didn't hide.

They showed up -- earlier, louder, and stronger than ever before.

_But not without cost. _

**Let me tell you more about what our students have been up against so far this year... **

In Maryland, one of our high school leaders -- just 17 years old -- helped organize a Club America event on campus back in December.

It was peaceful. Students only. Parental permission required. No outside adults. Everything done by the book.

And yet, weeks later, during a recent local school board meeting...

A local woman stood up and publicly accused this student of "grooming children."

Then she went even further.

She told the board: _" All members of this Board are mandatory reporters... Based on the circumstances surrounding this event, **a report was made to Child Protective Services. " **_

Yes, you read that right -- she weaponized CPS against one of our students.

Filed against a **minor. **

For organizing a pro-America Turning Point USA event with his friends.

Now, I want you to imagine being 17 years old... doing everything right... following every rule... showing up with courage and conviction...

And then hearing a stranger stand up in front of your entire community and imply that you're a danger to children.

That you need to be investigated. That you're the problem.

clean_body: One of the most hostile semesters Turning Point USA students have ever faced. | | | | | Fellow Patriot, I have to say it... The campus climate this spring? It 's been downright ugly. To be frank, the Left has never made it easy for our students. That's always come with the territory when you're speaking truth deep in the belly of the beast... But this semester is different. This has been one of the most hostile semesters Turning Point USA students have ever faced. From coast to coast, high school and college students who dared to stand for faith, freedom, and this great nation have been stalked, slandered, threatened, and in some cases -- physically attacked. All for saying what you and I know to be true: That America is worth defending. That speech must remain free. And that Charlie Kirk's life and legacy meant something. And despite the opposition -- our students didn't back down. They didn't run. They didn't hide. They showed up -- earlier, louder, and stronger than ever before. But not without cost. Let me tell you more about what our students have been up against so far this year... In Maryland, one of our high school leaders -- just 17 years old -- helped organize a Club America event on campus back in December. It was peaceful. Students only. Parental permission required. No outside adults. Everything done by the book. And yet, weeks later, during a recent local school board meeting... A local woman stood up and publicly accused this student of "grooming children." Then she went even further. She told the board: " All members of this Board are mandatory reporters... Based on the circumstances surrounding this event, a report was made to Child Protective Services. " Yes, you read that right -- she weaponized CPS against one of our students. Filed against a minor. For organizing a pro-America Turning Point USA event with his friends. Now, I want you to imagine being 17 years old... doing everything right... following every rule... showing up with courage and conviction... And then hearing a stranger stand up in front of your entire community and imply that you're a danger to children. That you need to be investigated. That you're the problem. Above: "Nancy" -- the Leftist Karen who filed a CPS report against a local Club America chapter and spoke out against them at a recent school board meeting. How would you respond? Because I'll tell you what he did... He walked up to that microphone -- calm, steady, unshaken -- and said: " We have been accused of many things... I'm the president of the group. I'm 17, I'm a minor. I can't groom children because I am a child." Seventeen years old. Standing alone. But standing strong in front of his entire community while facing outrageous, malicious accusations. That's courage. The kind of courage Charlie would've been proud of. And that courage is catching fire across the country. But so is the hatred. Because what happened in Maryland wasn't an isolated incident... It's just the beginning: 🚨 At Lawrence University in Wisconsin, Leftists on campus are trying to permanently shut down a brand-new TPUSA chapter before it even starts. Never mind that Lawrence has over 160 student clubs... and not one is right-leaning. Or that the university handbook bans discrimination based on political affiliation. One of our students there is now receiving death threats. And instead of protecting him? The Left-wing student government is putting the chapter's fate up to a campus-wide vote. 🚨 At Iowa State University, Colby Brandt -- the student body president -- was threatened with impeachment because he had connections to TPUSA. Fortunately, his "impeachment" was dismissed by the student government's judicial branch... But this was only after the outrage that followed on social media and the university's administration came to its senses. 🚨 At Worcester Polytechnic, one of our signs that featured a quote with Charlie was vandalized with the phrase: "he should've ducked ahole." 🚨 At Lake Zurich High School, one of our students held an "I ❤️ ICE" sign -- and was physically threatened by a peer. On school grounds and caught on camera. 🚨 At the University of Houston, a Leftist mocked Charlie Kirk's assassination while harassing TPUSA students at a tabling event on campus -- wishing cancer and paralysis on their families while making sexual gestures. 🚨 And at Coastal Carolina Community College, a professor was recorded saying this in front of his class: "Did he (Charlie Kirk) deserve to die? No... but..." Then he added: " He was a racist piece of st. And Turning Point USA is a racist piece of st organization." The message was clear. I could go on and on with more examples of the Left's hatred towards our students... But while they mock Charlie's death, encourage hate, harassment, and try to poison students against the very ideas our country was built on... In the face of all this -- our students aren 't folding. Not one bit. They're still tabling at campus events. They're still meeting after school -- still recruiting, still growing. They're still passing out pocket Constitutions and American flags. They're still launching chapters in hostile territory -- places where they've been told, outright, that they're not welcome. And while their peers stage "ICE Walkouts" and chaos in the halls... Our students are gathering to pray -- for their schools, for law enforcement, and for this nation -- quietly around their school's flagpole. That's because these students made a decision -- the same decision Charlie challenged them to every day: " It doesn't take skill to be courageous. It takes a choice." They chose courage. They chose to stand for faith, freedom, and family. They chose to defend everything that makes this country worth fighting for. They truly are the courageous generation. In fact, since Charlie 's assassination last September: 🔥 Over 140,000 students raised their hands to get involved 🔥 4,600+ active chapters are now operating across America 🔥 More than 1 million students are part of this movement And Fellow Patriot, patriots like you are the reason they've been able to do it... Because while the Left mocked Charlie's death-- while the hate followed and the attacks intensified -- you didn't disappear. Patriots like you stood firm. You stood with these students. You made it clear: The mission doesn 't end here. And now, because of your faithfulness, we 're watching the seeds Charlie planted come to life in high schools, colleges, and communities across this country. Our students may not know your name... But they know someone made it possible for them to take a stand on their campus. They're walking into classrooms bolder than ever. Speaking truth in places where lies once ruled. Because someone gave them the chance. That someone was you. Patriots like you reminded these students that they're not alone -- even when it feels like it. You helped push back the darkness. You made space for courage to grow. The kind of courage Charlie lived for. The kind of courage he gave everything for. So, thank you, Fellow Patriot. Thank you for giving these young patriots a fighting chance. We will not stop. We will not retreat. We will keep standing for truth -- louder and stronger than ever before. Because Charlie's mission didn't end with his life. It's being carried forward -- by thousands of students... and by you. And that 's the one thing the Left can't stand. Let's keep pushing. Let's keep growing. Let's keep going -- together. | | For Charlie, Justin Streiff Chief Operating Officer Turning Point USA P.S. Fellow Patriot, thank you again for taking a stand for our brave students. It's truly incredible watching these students from across the country lining up to start the next wave of new Turning Point chapters. They're watching what's happening... seeing the attacks... hearing the hate from the Left... And still saying: " Sign me up." All they need? A little backup. Every new chapter receives a full activism kit from Turning Point USA, filled with everything they need to lead boldly: ✅ Pocket Constitutions ✅ American Flags ✅ Chapter Leadership Tools ✅ Organizing Guides ✅ Patriotic TPUSA Gear Each one costs just $25 to send to a student chapter. You don't need to start a chapter yourself. But you can help a new one get off the ground. And you can be the reason a kid on a hostile campus doesn't feel like they're fighting alone. ** 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

name: Ken Martin
subject: Iran:
body:
---
Derek, Overnight and without congressional approval, Donald Trump initiated major combat operations against Iran. Trump himself said that this operation is “massive and ongoing” and he expects there may be American casualties. I am praying for the safety of our men and women in uniform, of Americans and their families in the region, and of innocent civilians. Trump sold voters on a “pro-peace” vision of himself as an America First candidate, yet in under 13 months, he has ordered strikes on seven foreign nations and plunged our country into more open-ended conflict using taxpayer dollars. While he’s distracted by foreign conflicts and shiny ballrooms, Trump has failed to deliver on his promise to bring costs down for working families, who are paying more every day because of Trump’s actions. **If we can’t trust Donald Trump to live up to his most basic promises here on the home front, how can we possibly trust his judgment to put our brave servicemembers in harm’s way?** Make no mistake: the Iranian regime has sanctioned terrorism, and undermined democracy and the human rights of its people. But our nation deserves better than a government that shoots first and asks questions later. Americans do not look fondly on presidents that force us into deadly, expensive, endless conflicts. Democrats in Congress are demanding answers on behalf of the American people, who have made clear they do not support Trump’s war. Ken Ken Martin
Chair
Democratic National Committee

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

Hey folks,
After Donald Trump launched another illegal war, I went live with my buddy Adam Mockler to break down what this means -- for our democracy, for our economy, and for young Americans who could be sent to fight in a war they never voted for. This is a must-watch conversation if you're trying to make sense of the chaos in real time.
Here are a few moments you don't want to miss:
* **[00:01:07]** Adam calls this the biggest betrayal of Trump's campaign promises -- after running on "no new wars," Trump launches an unforced conflict that immediately triggers regional retaliation.
* **[00:05:26]** We break down how tearing up the JCPOA nuclear deal set the stage for this escalation -- no backup plan, no strategy, just perpetual strikes and rising instability.
* **[00:10:16]** We read Trumpworld's own words -- from Stephen Miller to J.D. Vance -- promising young men they'd never be drafted under Trump. The hypocrisy is staggering.
* **[00:14:25]** The real question: what will Congress actually do? We talk about executive overreach, the War Powers Clause, and why Democrats must force a vote instead of issuing "strongly worded statements."
* **[00:23:03]** I lay out the bottom line: if Congress won't act and Trump ignores the courts, the final backstop is us -- voting, organizing, protesting, and electing leaders who understand how to use power responsibly.

clean_body: "Regime Change" is a great big lie. | | | Friend, On February 28, Donald Trump and Bibi Netanyahu launched a massive unprovoked bombing campaign inside Iran. , Trump said he started this war, and Americans are likely to die. "The lives of courageous American heroes may be lost, and we may have casualties. That often happens in war." The Constitution requires Congress to declare war. Trump's war is therefore illegal. It is also likely to be a "forever war " because Trump made clear he wants "regime change." History is not on Trump's side. When nations are attacked and killed by foreigners, they inevitably rally behind their leaders - no matter how much they hate them. And on day 1, US-Israeli bombs hit a girls' elementary school in Minab . As we learned so painfully in both Vietnam and Iraq, killing people does not win their "hearts and minds" - it only hardens their resolve to fight back. That's what makes war so deadly and expensive. Iran is a nation of 93 million people. When George W. Bush invaded Iraq, its population was only 26 million. Just six weeks after the invasion, Bush infamously declared "Mission Accomplished." Bush lied - Americans fought and died for another 8 years. This week, Congress is likely to vote on a War Powers Resolution demanded by Democrats and a handful of constitutionalist Republicans. Thank for all you do! Bob Fertik, President Democrats.com p.s. Opposing Trump will take a strong and determined organizing effort so your contribution of any amount will make a huge difference. I'll have more to say soon about what this moment will require of us. We are going to keep standing up, speaking out, and supporting the next generation of progressive leaders who will always stand up to fascists and oppose the forever wars that make all of us less safe.

David

* * *
Friend, This is not normal. During his State of the Union address, Donald Trump suggested **“it should be my third term”** and declared that the **“only way”** Democrats can win is to cheat. Now, Trump is escalating efforts to bend elections to his will ahead of November – while simultaneously undermining public trust in the outcome.
* He’s called to “nationalize” elections, even though the Constitution leaves election administration to the states.
* His Justice Department is suing states for private voter roll data.
* The FBI has seized ballots from 2020 in Georgia.
* And Trump himself has said he will only accept the 2026 results “if the elections are honest.”

That’s not how democracy works. In America, voters decide elections. Not presidents. Not the Department of Justice. | | Hi there,

I’m reaching out personally to ask you to make a quick donation to my campaign for Georgia governor before **tonight's midnight deadline.**

I hope you’ll give me a moment to explain why your support _today_ is so important. If you’re ready to make a contribution, you can pitch in here: _**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/geoff-duncan-202602-em](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126346943/604698933/985402107?firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&addr1=&city=Cresco&state=PA&zip=18326&phone=&employer=&occupation=&amount=25&refcode=EM_RTI_GD_20260228_FR_2G_T1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA3MDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYzBiNDA2NzEtY2YxNC1mMTExLWE2OWEtMDAwZDNhNTc1OTNmIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=cvc5kIf4GG9iAyYS4HKEY4uQQoJLfXC4ZolCSaIzgZU=)**_

Quite frankly, we’ve hit a make-or-break moment for our campaign. It’s been nearly 30 years since Georgia elected a Democratic governor, and I know I’m the one candidate who can build a big enough tent to reverse that trend.

_But we only have a couple of weeks left to make our message heard._

name: Alycia R. Gruenhagen | U.S. Senate 2026
subject: Term Limits: I Don’t Plan on Serving More Than One Term
body:
Fellow Minnesotan to Fellow Minnesotan.

| | | | | [|
---](https://gmail.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3aa86647bf142972a85274d7e&id=656316ca17&e=49d94faf06)
| | | | [|
---](https://gmail.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3aa86647bf142972a85274d7e&id=7ce4cb50e1&e=49d94faf06)
| | **Term Limits: I Don't Plan on Serving More Than One Term (Key Issues)**

---
| |

Friends,
As things stand today, **I don’t plan on serving more than one term.** My intention at this point is to serve faithfully and then to let the voice of the people speak.
That said, I am a firm believer in freedom. If the people decide they want to elect the same person again, I believe that voice should be heard. Restricting the people’s right to choose their representative is not, in my view, aligned with the principles of liberty.
**The real concern many are raising isn’t truly about term limits — it’s about campaign finance.** Outside money and large donors can distort the process, making it harder to ensure that elected officials are accountable to the people rather than special interests. On that issue, I agree: we should be focused on meaningful campaign finance limits **so that the people’s voice — not big-dollar influence — drives elections.**
**Additionally, I believe unelected bureaucrats appointed to lead departments should absolutely have term limits.** The public does not get the opportunity to vote on these individuals, and we should not be locked into long-term appointments without accountability.
I hope this clarifies my position. My views on the issues are outlined on my website, and I’ve attached a shorter version in flyer format for your reference. **Since 2015 I have been a supporter of President Donald J. Trump.**[**TRUMP has far exceeded my expectations and I enthusiastically support his agenda to Make America Great Again**](https://gmail.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3aa86647bf142972a85274d7e&id=ff248c2515&e=49d94faf06)**.** If you didn't see his State of the Union Address I would suggest you watch it.
Please let me know if there’s anything further you’d like to discuss. [Email, text or chat with me on my website. ](https://gmail.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3aa86647bf142972a85274d7e&id=2a7de68f96&e=49d94faf06)
Best regards,
**Alycia R. Gruenhagen** **Candidate for U.S. Senate, Minnesota** Glencoe, MN **www.alycia4senate.com** Proudly representing OUR SHARED Minnesota values.
---
