subject: Delegate Sewell's February Newsletter
body:
| |
---
# District 25 February Newsletter
---
|
---
Dear Inquirer,
---
|
---
Over the past month and a half of the 2026 legislative session, it has been my honor to serve you in the Virginia General Assembly. Together, with the thoughtful insight of engaged constituents, advocacy organizations, young leaders, and community partners, my staff and I are turning your priorities into action. It is a privilege to fight for you and your family, and I am deeply grateful for the thousands of emails, calls, and in-person conversations that continue to shape this work. Your voices guide every vote I take.
---
This has been a busy and productive legislative session. More than 1,500 bills were introduced in the House of Delegates, and 853 have advanced to the Senate. I am proud to share that nine of the bills I introduced have passed the House and are continuing through the legislative process. My responsibility is to represent your voice, and each of these bills was inspired by conversations in our community, from making housing more affordable, to expanding access to higher education and workforce development, addressing the child care shortage, and advancing paid family and medical leave for hardworking Virginians.
---
It remains an incredible honor to represent Virginia’s 25th District, and I am excited to share an update on our progress. In this newsletter, you will find:
* A summary and breakdown of the legislation I’ve introduced
* Updates on key bills moving through the General Assembly
* Photos of the incredible constituents and advocates who stopped by to share their stories

---
**2026 Legislative Agenda**
---
|
---
|
---
Below, you will find a summary of each bill I introduced to make Virginia a more **affordable, safe, and community-focused** place to live. That is what you and our neighbors deserve and voted for. **Delivering on Affordability for You**
* [**HB1207 - Paid Family and Medical Leave**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/dHViVMnmChGxDCSLZaYzjw~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPllooJ2_JxjZH1yZHr_sWtTPHzeF0p6RAASfgqLnrW14qKgM7eHdl2ius3rBHGjweIbbDW23OMUc2PCXXaJ56i8w~~)
* Eighty-four percent of Virginians support establishing a paid family and medical leave program so that hardworking people can care for a loved one, welcome a new child, or recover from a serious illness without fear of losing a paycheck or their job. This legislation reflects that overwhelming consensus. It is good for workers, good for families, and good for Virginia’s businesses and economy. Paid leave is a tested, proven policy that strengthens workforce participation, improves employee retention, and provides stability when families need it most.

I was honored that Abigail Spanberger expressed support for this bill in her address to the Joint Assembly, and I am proud that the House of Delegates has passed it. The bill is now scheduled to be heard in the Senate on Monday afternoon, and I remain committed to seeing it across the finish line for Virginia families.
* [**HB1208 - Child Care Funding Formula Clarification**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/76OpoL2A55kLG9bQ-8gGhA~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPln2aq1aPAl_GNQ4KJQ7OxQARAhk9qa8wC6iraNPf9-r9hjmDxZBqk5cV1_WyY8fnEiFlbZZMCfz3bEp5pfRVAsQ~~)
* Childcare remains a significant economic barrier for families in Virginia and limits both parents’ ability to remain in the workforce. Yet, the commonwealth lacks a transparent and reliable way of determining the level of care funding needed year over year to support our families and expand access. This bill establishes a childcare access calculator that incorporates three critical components.

1. The calculation **_predicts_** slots needed for program eligibility across Virginia's public early childhood and education programs.
2. The calculation **_quantifies_** the pre-child cost of delivering quality care across programs, age groups, and regions; and
3. The calculation **_identifies_** additional slots needed to ensure supply keeps pace with economic activity and workforce needs.

I am pleased to share that the bill has passed the House of Delegates and will soon be considered by the state Senate.
* [**HB1221 - Reform and Streamlining of VA Higher Education Grants**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/_r3OqHsmxVn71eehmQ3E1g~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPl9Q1ULYtaxeI0vZyWGYwYnGE2oLNNgeCUpg63bTl9btacZIccp-OzrSq8MPWuepXgR3KVoYjA4ECEUEv1jh9fOA~~)
* Virginia has many excellent colleges and universities that help students shape their futures. Educational grants help make college more affordable for students with financial challenges. This bill will expand access to Virginia Educational Grants for students who need financial support and are keeping up with their studies. I am happy to share that the bill has passed the House of Delegates and is now headed to the state Senate.

* [**HB1210 - Capital Gains Tax Freeze on Residential Homes**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/bzYau3uz4Lh-6DEXNMrGJg~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlhRmc4uUnCXg-MTa-WNeq7b6i6utmDYFlUZxQ1JMhcBwEbtDAyp76vc3jk_8Lx_A3BCLJ6nneQIYbfh5XA21TmA~~)
* To provide tax relief to homeowners looking to sell the home and find their new one, I introduced legislation to shield homeowners from state tax on capital gains. This will increase flexibility for homeowners, so they aren’t burdened by Virginia state taxes on selling their primary residence. Unfortunately, this bill did not pass, but I am committed to making housing affordable for Virginia residents. I am excited to announce that this bill has passed the House of Delegates.
* [**HB 1211 - First Time Homebuyer Tax Credit**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/pGZsXDpjXejykGVoGGbYWQ~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlHjVhOHDRvqIYtgg_2jCBWwFeJJZAfwynx2IJqK3a4o7P1S6lC6b8mpGHuzYsh2tO7vW9e0mnZguENUdcBw95Ew~~)
* Owning a home helps create stability, build wealth for future generations, and strengthen our communities. These are goals we all share. That is why I introduced a bill to give first-time homebuyers a tax credit. Making housing affordable is key to helping families grow and keeping opportunities open in Virginia. Although this bill did not pass, I remain committed to making housing more affordable for everyone in our state.
* [**HB 1212 - Small Lot Homebuilding Ordinance**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/R0zTTwCOUnTzZg-LYC3mYg~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlYcGJjzejN8zP9q2El6QDb4b91hIdGXPtsks4FFX8LNQYutU2AEyy9xRBTxul0owFAs7cmFAhcz6xx9VSd7lMxA~~)
* Every family deserves access to a home that fits their needs and their budget. That’s why I introduced legislation to ensure localities have the authority to support the rapid development of housing on smaller lots, a practical, community-focused strategy to expand our housing supply. By giving local governments the tools to increase housing stock, this bill promotes affordability, creates more options for working families, seniors, and young people just starting out, and helps ensure that Virginians can find a home that’s right for them at every stage of life. I am happy to share that this legislation has passed the House of Delegates and will be taken up by the State Senate next week. I look forward to continuing the work to make housing more accessible and attainable across our Commonwealth.

**Keeping our Commonwealth Safe**
* [**HB1219 - Drone as a First Responder**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/mnZgd-VHI2lwf4jWNE487Q~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlHUP4q58vCH_obzXWoWCShP2Qg4fnkX3Dn7pG6tKHMzUXp1D_Brq4c-2hBfTF-zwC9Id9zXIm9M1dd8qbS8c_8Q~~)
* To strengthen public safety and emergency response, this bill streamlines the process for law enforcement to obtain search warrants for drone deployment. Drones enhance real-time situational awareness, aid in crime scene assessments, and expedite the delivery of emergency supplies. This bill has the potential to save lives by fast-tracking communication between the scene and emergency responder support. I am excited to announce that this bill has passed the House of Delegates.
* [**HB1446 - Training School Nurses to Recognize Symptoms of Sickle Cell Anemia**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/UYVMMRw8ipxKjT8L8Pnyzw~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlDmyfUatMlrqyt0rikedcYSe6U9WwDG1uT3MjIeIOkExlJ-UpS0ruHrmPQ1ndczrO1a2ZxeeNGMwXG3GJCHl9Jw~~)
* School nurses are the most important healthcare professionals in some students' lives. Children all across Virginia depend on their school nurse when they feel hurt. Sickle Cell Anemia can cause significant pain and health problems for people with the disease. The legislation I put forth requires that school nurses complete training to recognize the signs of sickle cell disease. It’s my privilege to announce that this bill has passed the House of Delegates.

**Sustainability and Preservation**
* [**HB1230 - Incentivizing Sustainable Aviation Fuel Production in Virginia**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/Ne55NNVz2h4-LkjDrFYb8w~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPl5BXDAwwmCINz-PcNOM0lv5o-x3-YkbQsnO4vR-y035D_a1CQcCnBWoyR1yRuvYnThK_Gicr2viHfJ1H61WeuPQ~~)
* Our agricultural community is being hit hard by tariffs and global market uncertainty. House Bill 1230 is designed to open the door to new, reliable markets for Virginia farmers whether through crops, oilseeds, or agricultural byproducts used in fuel production.

Instead of relying solely on volatile export markets, we can create demand right here at home. This bill is about giving farmers more financial certainty, strengthening rural economies, and making sure Virginia agriculture not only survives these unpredictable headwinds but grows through them. Unfortunately, this bill was carried over to 2027. While disappointing, the work will continue.
* [**HB1234 - Allowing for Increased Placement of Solar Panels in Large Lots**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/_70TlEjTRlU7QHH3ia6TwQ~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlFRfKTA6EpjPBFyQUkr91Xk_TefX05qMdcnE6Pl9VYHkr7H01sYJEWvdlI3NSjHxE7n20npSsE2PuFfa95qXOmg~~)
* Parking lots take up a large amount of space that's only utilized some of the time. The implementation of solar panels above parking lots may utilize empty space and create renewable energy, reducing overall energy demand. I'm working to allow localities to require nonresidential parking lots to install solar panels, and allow the building to use the electricity for its own purposes. I am excited to announce that this bill has passed the House of Delegates.
* [**HB1237 - Enabling the Preservation of Neglected Private Cemeteries**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/8n_wolZHxUdwL2PZsfpKQQ~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlO4tLvDgUDlUcbsIXIjSfd6dJb6czcdNW4O80OwMz9AhqHbA-A3tZ6CEgUHZQ5W9RHaO5I4s5scRZFq6Dg-U_bQ~~)
* Virginia has an extraordinarily deep history, rich with historical significance. Because of our long history, some historical areas such as cemeteries have become neglected. These cemeteries require maintenance in order to preserve our history. The legislation I introduced will allow a petitioner to care for the preservation of neglected cemeteries with unknown owners. I am pleased to share that this bill has passed the House of Delegates. Thank you to the Prince William Historical Commission for the bill suggestion and for entrusting me to deliver upon your request.

**Keeping our Commonwealth Connected**
* [**HB1226 - Private College License Plate Outreach**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/PIrV6fzLZwc3q0jSkHwfrw~~/AAS2yhA~/mDPybghYAWqYP_QuHoXsezfaWjHa7LJ96I9ziCLEqG03jtp6pGbJJlC_RQPKCYPlINp-UjScrxRMBF0jLI-S37IXeX_8HcbD6qOtFuik7ta2WdQhKVEPZk76d71qc7nk1urVc6xFDulihwokaJxQJw~~)
* Virginian’s abundant higher education opportunities have created a workforce of proud alumni that display their university on their license plate. This bill would allow drivers to choose to share their choice of license plate with their college so that they can stay connected with the college’s outreach efforts. I am excited to report that this bill has passed the House of Delegates and state Senate with unanimous support.

---
**Notable Bills from Other Legislators**
---
* [**HB1 - Raising the Minimum Wage**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/d_McKtmVJ7RCPm6qzU2WVg~~/AAS2yhA~/aXWXMwcqjTIXzgKsgYnsxZ97O0nnuJnvaI6EakLOLeYfW6Elo8pM0Rcwi5yxxvaFiHlat7nF32dnYtS7KuOkLA2JgKacmpgHC5tYZ_aqM3XQK_20rQfkkcXWvrQR4JYD9pznDoaWaZtZKe65NPqPGQ~~)
* This bill incrementally raises the Virginia minimum wage to $15 an hour in 2028. This legislation makes sure that Virginians that work hard can reap the benefits and afford to stay in our beautiful commonwealth.

* [**HB2 - Making Energy More Affordable**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/dOS3ai8AnInPWbb3fse12A~~/AAS2yhA~/aXWXMwcqjTIXzgKsgYnsxZ97O0nnuJnvaI6EakLOLeYfW6Elo8pM0Rcwi5yxxvaFI5MGlSGNTWDww50B-qOG6CjYhxhnlGKSMoBMmVEbwMJd_i51zweHLk_8krVJnOD9yZ2Ycx97JrTyD8SMBwfR7A~~)
* This bill requires Dominion Energy and Appalachian Power to identify and implement stricter energy efficient policies and identify cost-saving measures for consumers. That means more money in your pocket!

* [**HB5 - Paid Sick Leave for Home Health Workers**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/eTPxfBd6j-_w5yIGy07gfw~~/AAS2yhA~/aXWXMwcqjTIXzgKsgYnsxZ97O0nnuJnvaI6EakLOLeYfW6Elo8pM0Rcwi5yxxvaF3NXABtKtk4azIRn3UjBPAk6dg1wdh6ULMVsmmaaX95EUkUd7JIWAg1q550-MNMOJ55wXeJQbyQCy26JaUCk_IA~~)****
* This bill expands paid sick leave to most employees in Virginia, ensuring workers can earn and use leave for illness, family care, or situations involving domestic violence. This legislation protects workers’ rights, holds employers accountable with penalties for violations, and allows employees to recover unpaid leave.

* [**HB484 - Preventing Automatic Downcoding in Medical Billing**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/624IQnNM97Jxl7g4P50viQ~~/AAS2yhA~/qicGZDZ8tckG36zJGnX8_kmyZvgdGINsjdI7KenREUAk0nWugveMoIQ8g_dKuxhexuRxCL9IKt2XOBbchXJQMfurfbtayJV_uWcVvxNUJIsb-xHCr2eAGI_jQo_3VwxOZfK4m-DGwairs_uxgQZYhg~~)
* This bill prevents automatic downcoding in medical billing. Downcoding is a practice in which a lower reimbursement code is applied to a medical insurance claim, resulting in a lower rate of reimbursement. HB484 requires that any downcode is made with cause and documentation, and makes a clear path for disputing the decision to downcode.

* [**HJ1 - Referendum on Enshrining Reproductive Freedom**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/8crqmmEUP8ZbdYCflR_S9Q~~/AAS2yhA~/aXWXMwcqjTIXzgKsgYnsxZ97O0nnuJnvaI6EakLOLeYfW6Elo8pM0Rcwi5yxxvaF00hfOpyNUsCX8CueeLd7EPL3LC0X7kJ5sS1L5sAY6kQ5tDKX0xaw9hvsUIm_XaVyoQc7FalNIF44nB20iqJTKA~~)
* Every Virginian deserves the right to choose when to start their family. Virginia shines as a beacon of freedom and individual choice and with this legislation, Virginians will have the opportunity to enshrine that right.

* [**HJ2 - Referendum on Automatic Restoration of Voting Rights**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/_bgxenI78ADXKUM7Bpdb1g~~/AAS2yhA~/aXWXMwcqjTIXzgKsgYnsxZ97O0nnuJnvaI6EakLOLeYfW6Elo8pM0Rcwi5yxxvaFtc0hsRBo5It-odJEujX0xZRt31tozwZjBA0c7wd3hJCP8s_p4VA6K75QExl4lzcUcW700xRl7j0zFjH6JFcEWA~~)
* To strengthen our commonwealth’s commitment to equal voting rights, this legislation would restore the right to vote to all Virginians who have been released from incarceration. Virginians returning citizens deserve the opportunity to reintegrate into our communities and engaging in the political process is a key component.

* [**HJ3 - Referendum on Enshrining the Right to Marry**](https://go.sparkpostmail.com/f/a/yQtB57FTSuq3kajDpyOKKw~~/AAS2yhA~/aXWXMwcqjTIXzgKsgYnsxZ97O0nnuJnvaI6EakLOLeYfW6Elo8pM0Rcwi5yxxvaFqJGZnyv7zRJCecjIimwM2q1ogGR0UZov0VffAhjCT8uoxtApo2_TUprF_HPUaZMNIUh2FyqS1knrd7DVMjBT9w~~)
* Marriage is a sacred and personal expression of love and commitment. It is highly important to protect two adults' right to marry regardless of sex, gender, or race.

---
It cannot be overstated how incredibly grateful I am for the constituents and advocates who have supported these bills. Your voices and engagement make all the difference. Please do not hesitate to make your voice heard. That is the reason why I am here. If you would like to speak in support or opposition of any bills in committee, please reach out to **delbsewell@house.virginia.gov** for information.

I am sincerely grateful to every constituent, advocacy group, and leader who has come to my office to make their voice heard.

**News You Can Use**
---
**According to the nonpartisan Tax Foundation, Trump’s tariffs amounted to an average tax increase of $1,000 per U.S. household in 2025. That cost is expected to climb to $1,300 per household this year — and if these policies remain in place, tariff-driven price increases could cost the average family $1,700 next year.** Seventy-one percent of Americans report spending more on groceries than they did last year. In 2026, tariffs continue to function as a significant indirect tax on American families, driving up consumer prices by billions of dollars annually and reducing purchasing power. Although these taxes are paid by U.S. importers, the costs are passed directly on to consumers, raising prices on everyday essentials like food, clothing, electronics, baby formula, and diapers. Low-income families are hit hardest, as they spend a larger share of their income on these goods. **Here in Virginia, I am proud to report that neither chamber’s budget proposes new taxes** on our working families. My colleagues and I remain focused on lowering costs and improving quality of life. In our next newsletter, I’ll share more about the bipartisan budget passed by the Virginia House of Delegates and how it works to make life more affordable for every household.

Keeping our Commonwealth Connected ~~ Virginian’s abundant higher education opportunities have created a workforce of proud alumni that display their university on their license plate. This bill would allow drivers to choose to share their choice of license plate with their college so that they can stay connected with the college’s outreach efforts. I am excited to report that this bill has passed the House of Delegates and state Senate with unanimous support. Notable Bills from Other Legislators ~~ This bill incrementally raises the Virginia minimum wage to $15 an hour in 2028. This legislation makes sure that Virginians that work hard can reap the benefits and afford to stay in our beautiful commonwealth. ~~ This bill requires Dominion Energy and Appalachian Power to identify and implement stricter energy efficient policies and identify cost-saving measures for consumers. That means more money in your pocket! ~~** This bill expands paid sick leave to most employees in Virginia, ensuring workers can earn and use leave for illness, family care, or situations involving domestic violence. This legislation protects workers’ rights, holds employers accountable with penalties for violations, and allows employees to recover unpaid leave. ~~ This bill prevents automatic downcoding in medical billing. Downcoding is a practice in which a lower reimbursement code is applied to a medical insurance claim, resulting in a lower rate of reimbursement. HB484 requires that any downcode is made with cause and documentation, and makes a clear path for disputing the decision to downcode. ~~ Every Virginian deserves the right to choose when to start their family. Virginia shines as a beacon of freedom and individual choice and with this legislation, Virginians will have the opportunity to enshrine that right. ~~ To strengthen our commonwealth’s commitment to equal voting rights, this legislation would restore the right to vote to all Virginians who have been released from incarceration. Virginians returning citizens deserve the opportunity to reintegrate into our communities and engaging in the political process is a key component. ~~ Marriage is a sacred and personal expression of love and commitment. It is highly important to protect two adults' right to marry regardless of sex, gender, or race. It cannot be overstated how incredibly grateful I am for the constituents and advocates who have supported these bills. Your voices and engagement make all the difference. Please do not hesitate to make your voice heard. That is the reason why I am here. If you would like to speak in support or opposition of any bills in committee, please reach out to delbsewell@house.virginia.gov for information. Visitors in the Office I am sincerely grateful to every constituent, advocacy group, and leader who has come to my office to make their voice heard. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Events in and Around the 25th District Reading to Dogs Date: Varying dates Address: Independent Hill Library; 14418 Bristow Road Manassas VA Time: 10:00am- 11:00am (certain days may have different times) Additional Details: Practice reading aloud with a new dog friend! Come to Independent Hill library to read to a therapy dog. All ages welcome! Visit for exact times and dates. Mobile Market Date: Monday, March 2 Address: 2201 Opitz Boulevard Woodbridge, VA, 22191 Time: 4:00pm- 6:00pm Additional Details: In collaboration with Capital Area Food Bank, Potomac Library will host a food market for those in need. Fresh produce will be provided on a first-come, first-served basis. Families are encouraged to bring their own bags. This event will be held in the Potomac Library Community room. Dale City Farmers Market Date: Sundays, March 1, March 8, and beyond Address: 14090 Gemini Way, Dale City, VA Time: 10:00am- 1:00pm Additional Details: No animals are allowed at both markets with the exception of service animals. News You Can Use According to the nonpartisan Tax Foundation, Trump’s tariffs amounted to an average tax increase of $1,000 per U.S. household in 2025. That cost is expected to climb to $1,300 per household this year — and if these policies remain in place, tariff-driven price increases could cost the average family $1,700 next year. Seventy-one percent of Americans report spending more on groceries than they did last year. In 2026, tariffs continue to function as a significant indirect tax on American families, driving up consumer prices by billions of dollars annually and reducing purchasing power. Although these taxes are paid by U.S. importers, the costs are passed directly on to consumers, raising prices on everyday essentials like food, clothing, electronics, baby formula, and diapers. Low-income families are hit hardest, as they spend a larger share of their income on these goods. Here in Virginia, I am proud to report that neither chamber’s budget proposes new taxes on our working families. My colleagues and I remain focused on lowering costs and improving quality of life. In our next newsletter, I’ll share more about the bipartisan budget passed by the Virginia House of Delegates and how it works to make life more affordable for every household. Hitting this goal means we can stay organized, communicate directly with voters, and run a serious, people-powered campaign in a moment when democracy itself feels under strain.

If you’re able, will you chip in $5 or $25 before the end of the month to help us reach $20,000 and keep this fight strong?

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

clean_body: This February, I spent time in DC and at home working for our values. | | | | February was a busy month. In Congress, I demanded ICE oversight and accountability, voted to protect affordable health care, and voted to end Trump's tariffs on Canada — addressing rising costs and affordability in Northwest Washington. I also spent time back home, in the district, listening to you and the community. At the start of the month, I toured a new development in Oak Harbor for affordable housing. Accessible and affordable housing is a cornerstone of thriving communities, but for too many working families and veterans nationwide, housing insecurity is front of mind. We need to tackle this head-on to ensure that everyone has a safe and affordable place to call home. Projects like the new affordable housing community in Oak Harbor are critical for Northwest Washington to tackle affordability and rising costs of living. This month, I also secured $10.1 million in federal funding for local projects in Northwest Washington. The federal funding will help create jobs, build community centers and strengthen infrastructure in Northwest Washington. Each investment of federal dollars here at home will serve our communities for decades to come. I will keep working closely with local leaders to make sure federal spending benefits the communities I represent. This February, I also had the opportunity to celebrate Valentine's Day in a very special way. This year, I launched an annual Valentines for Veterans drive. To all the women and men who have served our country, I hope they had a happy Valentine's Day, and I thank them for their service. [ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

We woke up to chilling news: overnight, Donald Trump launched "major
combat operations" against Iran – dragging us headlong into a catastrophic
war the American people NEVER authorized.

This is Trump launching us into war without public debate, without
Congressional authorization, and without the consent of the people who
will pay the price. But Congress still has the power – and the
responsibility – to stop this. Now, Schumer is calling for Congress to
return to DC to move up a vote on the War Powers vote ASAP.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35873?source=email-20230228&t=1011&akid=10300%2E5885482%2Eaajhwp ]Headline: Lawmakers ramp up push for war powers resolution after US
strikes Iran

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35873?source=email-20230228&t=1012&akid=10300%2E5885482%2Eaajhwp ]Congress can stop this – but only if each of us demands action NOW.
Will you send an urgent message to your members of Congress to immediately
vote to end Trump's war with Iran and restore peace?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35873?source=email-20230228&t=1013&akid=10300%2E5885482%2Eaajhwp ]ADD YOUR NAME

We've seen this nightmare before. Vietnam. Iraq. Afghanistan. Decades of
endless wars that cost trillions, killed hundreds of thousands of innocent
people, and left our nation no safer. We cannot let history repeat itself
because of Trump's desperate bid to distract from his own failures.

Already, dozens of lives have been tragically lost. And Trump just warned,
"the lives of courageous American heroes may be lost and we may have
casualties. That often happens in war..."

Even members of Trump's MAGA base are condemning this strike. Tucker
Carlson called it "absolutely disgusting and evil."

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35873?source=email-20230228&t=1014&akid=10300%2E5885482%2Eaajhwp ]Headline: MAGA melts down over iran war no one voted for

Now Schumer is calling for senators to assemble for a vote on the War
Powers Act. The House is already set to vote on a companion resolution
next week, led by Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie — which would reassert
Congress’s constitutional authority and prohibit U.S. involvement in a war
with Iran unless Congress explicitly authorizes it.

We've seen this before. The lies. The escalation. The devastation. And the
trillions of public dollars siphoned away from healthcare, housing,
climate action, and education. Because endless war is a gift to weapons
manufacturers and defense contractors – and a disaster for working people
here at home and innocent civilians abroad.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35873?source=email-20230228&t=1015&akid=10300%2E5885482%2Eaajhwp ]Congress ALONE holds the power to declare war, not the president acting
on a whim. So here’s what you can do right now: Tell your members of
Congress: ‘No endless war, no blank check, no illegal action.’ Vote YES on
the War Powers Resolutions to stop Trump’s war on Iran.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35873?source=email-20230228&t=1016&akid=10300%2E5885482%2Eaajhwp ]ADD YOUR NAME

Our Revolution members have always stood for diplomacy over destruction
and peace over war. Trump's unilateral war-making must come to an end.
Together, let's make it happen.

When we organize, we win,

Our Revolution

| | Dear Friend,

How much do you know about the Electoral College?

It's an important topic, and one vital to our nation's future.

You see, a movement is growing, led by progressives but supported by many well-meaning Americans, to change the way we elect our president.

**Their goal: to get rid of the Electoral College altogether, and "move beyond" the Constitution and Declaration. **

Voter registration activity increased across the country. According to the team at National Voter Registration Day, New York recorded more registrations for their 2025 events than in 2024, and California saw similar increases. Earlier this fall it looked like voter participation was going to make a real jump, even in a so-called "off-year".
Then Election Day came. New Jersey had more voters turn out for a gubernatorial election than they had in 20 years. Crucial counties in Pennsylvania saw their highest turnout levels in almost 15 years. New York City reached a turnout percentage unseen in over five decades.
We can drive even higher levels of participation when voters understand the stakes and feel like their vote matters , just like it did last November. That's why our voter registration efforts are so important, and why we work on it all year long.

subject: I Stand with President Trump on Operation Epic Fury – Read My Statement
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Trey Trainor for Texas
body:
President Trump met the moment with Operation Epic Fury. As a veteran, I stand firmly with our Commander-in-Chief and troops. America is safer.

| | | | | [|
---](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=ddbe60093f&e=4d3fe76c62)
| | Peter,
As a candidate for Congress and a proud veteran of the United States Army Reserves, I want to share with you my full statement on the recent launch of **Operation Epic Fury** against the Iranian regime.
Dripping Springs, TX – The following may be attributed to me, Trey Trainor, Republican Candidate for TX-21:
_“As a proud veteran who served honorably in the United States Army Reserves, I know firsthand the profound sacrifices our men and women in uniform make every day to protect our nation and defend freedom around the world. We pray fervently that our troops are never placed in harm's way, yet we remain eternally grateful for their unwavering willingness to answer the call when duty demands it._
_**Operation Epic Fury represents a necessary and decisive response to the Iranian regime's long-standing aggression** —the world's leading state sponsor of terrorism that has killed Americans, attacked our allies, brutally oppressed its own people, and pursued nuclear weapons in defiance of international efforts to secure peace. President Trump has met this moment head-on, acting to neutralize imminent threats to America and our allies while opening the door for the Iranian people to reclaim their country and embrace self-determination._
_**I stand firmly with our Commander-in-Chief, our brave service members carrying out this mission** , and the goal of ending the mullahs' reign of terror without entangling the United States in endless conflict. Our military's strength and resolve, backed by strong leadership, give us the best chance to achieve a more secure world. To our troops and their families: thank you for your service and sacrifice. America is safer because of you._
_**God bless our military, God bless President Trump, and God bless the United States of America**.”_
This operation underscores the importance of having strong, decisive leadership in the White House and fighters in Congress who will back our military, support America First policies, and keep our nation safe without endless wars. As the only candidate in this race who has worked directly with President Trump since 2016 and fought the DC swamp from the inside, I am committed to ensuring TX-21 has a voice that stands firmly with our troops and our Commander-in-Chief.
Please keep our service members, their families, and our nation in your prayers during this critical time.
For America First, for our military, and for TX-21,
**Trey Trainor** Husband, Father of 6,Proven Conservative for TX-21

name: Virginians For Fair Elections
subject: Misinformation could win unless we act now!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Virginians for Fair Elections
body:
A new poll shows what happens when voters haven’t heard the facts yet.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260228-247&t=1&akid=247%2E12592%2EkTJnYN)
We always knew this fight would require real work.
As you know, Governor Spanberger signed off on new congressional district maps that would likely result in Democrats winning 10 of the 11 House seats in Virginia.
But a new poll — fielded before our campaign had fully ramped up — shows what happens when voters haven’t heard the facts yet. Right now, 52% of Virginians would vote NO on the Fair Elections Amendment which would implement these maps.
When voters are misinformed on what constitutional amendments do, they start behind. That’s not unusual. What matters is what happens next.
**That’s exactly why Virginians for Fair Elections was created.**
Across the Commonwealth, MAGA-aligned voices and partisan operatives are flooding the airwaves with confusion, half-truths, and fear. And when voters believe misinformation, even an issue grounded in transparency and fairness can fall behind.
The Fair Elections amendment ensures Virginians see the maps, understand them, and decide for themselves whether or not they should be implemented. We know that’s the right way to do politics.
But here’s the truth we can’t ignore: **We wouldn’t win if the vote were held today.**
That’s because confusion and bad information are running rampant in Virginia. And that’s why we must get accurate information in front of voters _right now._
Early voting starts _**March 6**_ , and we urgently need your help today. **[Can you chip in whatever you can to help us:](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260228_1.MWbbhT&amount=3&refcode=20260228-247&t=2&akid=247%2E12592%2EkTJnYN)**
* Counter misinformation with voter education
* Reach Virginians with straightforward explanations of what the amendment _really_ does
* And ensure this campaign reflects the will of the people, not the loudest noise?

**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260228_1.MWbbhT&amount=3&refcode=20260228-247&t=21&akid=247%2E12592%2EkTJnYN)**
We can still turn this around. But we need resources — and with just **6 days** until early voting — we need them today. Thank you for helping ensure democracy prevails over chaos in Virginia.
— Virginians for Fair Elections

[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_vafe_2026_footer?refcode=em&t=22&refcode2=247_12592_kTJnYN&akid=247%2E12592%2EkTJnYN)
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

name: The Flyover
subject: What Does the Internet Know About You?
body:
Have you ever searched for your personal information on Google or ChatGPT?

---
| | |
---
| |
# Saturday, February 28, 2026
---

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: 254 counties have been failed by Abbott’s leadership
body:
Every one of Texas’ 254 counties deserves leadership that works for them, not special interests.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
There are 254 counties in Texas. More than any other state in the country, and every single one of them has been failed by Greg Abbott’s leadership.
**[I’ll tell you more, but first, can you pitch in $2.54 — a penny for each of the 254 counties Abbott has let down — to help us reach our end-of-month fundraising goal?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1712?c0=em_ms_gh_20260228_1_eom.sNHLCy&refcode=em20260228-675&t=1&akid=675%2E299639%2EEAkvyP)**
[Donate $2.54](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1712?c0=em_ms_gh_20260228_1_eom.sNHLCy&refcode=em20260228-675&t=2&akid=675%2E299639%2EEAkvyP)
I’ve been on the ground all over our state on our No Te Dejes — Fight Back Tour. And in every county we’ve visited, voters are sharing a similar sentiment: they’re hungry for change, and another four years of Greg Abbott only threatens to offer more of the same.
From Rio Grande Valley to Houston and everywhere in between, Texans are talking about how much they’re struggling to make ends meet. Working families are being forced to choose between keeping the lights on and paying sky high health care premiums. Parents are concerned about our neighborhood schools and the 5.5 million public school kids in our state who depend on them.
Everything they’ve shared tells us something I’ve known for a while: **Politics in Texas is broken.** _Nobody_ wants to keep the status quo, because it isn’t working for anyone except Abbott and his billionaire buddies.
This campaign is different. I don’t rely on corporate cash or billionaire donors, because I’m not interested in selling out hardworking Texans. Small dollar donations from grassroots supporters like you are the reason we can organize county by county and build a movement strong enough to win.
**[So, today I’m asking you to pitch in $2.54 for the 254 counties across Texas who are sick of politics as usual. Our end-of-month fundraising deadline is at midnight, and I need your support to keep me in this fight.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1712?c0=em_ms_gh_20260228_1_eom.sNHLCy&refcode=em20260228-675&t=3&akid=675%2E299639%2EEAkvyP)**

It’s time to elect a governor who truly works for Texans. Thank you for standing with me in this fight.
With gratitude,
Gina Hinojosa

I've seen it before.

_And I stopped it before._

**It started in 1998 when I was Speaker of the House.**

The Clinton Administration attempted to fundamentally corrupt the U.S. Census.

Their plan was called _" statistical sampling."_

**In plain English, it would have allowed unelected bureaucrats to manufacture population numbers instead of counting _real people, one at a time._**

Red states would be undercounted.
Blue states would be completely inflated.
Congressional seats would be rigged before a single vote was cast.

It was a direct assault on representative government, Peter.

_**So I sued Bill Clinton --and won.**_

It started in 1998 when I was Speaker of the House. The Clinton Administration attempted to fundamentally corrupt the U.S. Census. Their plan was called " statistical sampling." In plain English, it would have allowed unelected bureaucrats to manufacture population numbers instead of counting real people, one at a time. Red states would be undercounted. Blue states would be completely inflated. Congressional seats would be rigged before a single vote was cast. It was a direct assault on representative government, Peter. So I sued Bill Clinton --and won. The Supreme Court sided with me in a nail-biting 5-4 ruling. They agreed the only legitimate way to count the Census was by a strict, physical headcount. That victory protected the integrity of our elections for a generation. Now the same election scam is back. The Democrats are demanding tens of millions of Biden 's illegal aliens be counted in the Census. Not because it's lawful. Not because it's constitutional. But because it would permanently tilt political power in the Democrats' favor. Over thirty years in politics, and I can't recall a more brazen attempt to subvert the American system. And it 's happening right now in SOCIALIST SUPERSTATES like California and New York. These Democrats didn't roll out the red carpet for millions of illegals out of "compassion"... Republicans like you and me are now facing the most important midterm election of our lifetimes, and we have a clear choice to make: Are we going to let the Democrats STEAMROLL us through rigged Census counts? Or are we going to put U.S. elections back in the hands of U.S. citizens? Below is a petition calling for a CITIZENS ONLY CENSUS RECOUNT. We must put Congress in a pressure cooker. There's no bigger task than the task to secure our elections. Do NOT let the Democrats cheat their way to power. Do NOT let illegal aliens steal your vote. I know we can win this fight. I 've won it before - but I need you by my side. For America, Newt Gingrich Fmr. February 28, 2026
American woke up today with televised images of smoke emanating from Tehran from American bombs.
President Trump bombed Iran six months ago and claimed that their nuclear program had been destroyed. So why do we have to bomb Iran again?

Apparently President Trump believes that Iran still has the capacity to resurrect their nuclear program. He claims that Iran, if not deterred, will someday have nuclear-armed ballistic missiles that can not only strike American territory, but destroy Israel.

My Congressman, Democrat Jim Himes issued the following statement:

"Everything I have heard from the Administration before and after these strikes on Iran confirms this is a war of choice with no strategic endgame. As I expressed to Secretary Rubio when he briefed the Gang of Eight [Congressional leaders of both parties who are briefed on intelligence matters], military action in this region almost never ends well for the United States, and conflict with Iran can easily spiral and escalate in ways we cannot anticipate. It does not appear that Donald Trump has learned the lessons of history."

The Congressman is incorrect when he states this war has "no strategic endgame." President Trump stated that the military "should lay down their arms" and told the Iranian people that when the bombing stops "take over your government. It will be yours to take."

But this does not mean Congressman Himes is totally wrong. How are we going to make the Iranian military "lay down their arms?" Offer them tickets to Disneyland? And how are the Iranian people going to "take over [their] government" if the military does not lay down their arms? Slingshots? Bows and arrows? Thirty thousand Iranian citizens were shot and killed by the military during the recent rebellion against the Ayatollah.

First some quick background. Iran is the cradle of the oldest civilizations on the planet and to this day, is comprised of multiple ethic groups, the largest being the Persians, which is why the country was once called Persia. Its history is very complex but for the past few centuries, it was mostly controlled by leaders called shahs. But Iran edged towards democracy and by 1907, had its first Prime Minister. But in 1951, Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh nationalized British oil companies that invested heavily in Iran, and England along with the CIA arranged a coup that put Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi in power.

Under Pahlavi, Iran boomed. But the Shah was never popular and ruled brutally while perceived as an American puppet. Dissention increased and in 1979, the Carter administration allowed the Shah to be deposed and replaced with Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini. Iran was renamed the Islamic Republic of Iran and has been ruled by ayatollahs, Shiite Muslim religious leaders, to this day.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83cabf1f-8ea5-4c4e-ac82-6e254e2b6f43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Women of Tehran in the 1970s and Now

Shia law was imposed and Iran become a theocracy dedicated to spreading its religion throughout the Middle East. Internecine wars with Iraq (Sunni Muslims) resulted in over a million casualties. Iran is dedicated to destroying Israel and funds both Hezbollah and Hamas, Islamic groups that border Israel and foment attacks.

Thus the present mess. Which is why Congressman Himes warns the Trump administration "military action in this region almost never ends well for the United States."

At the time of this writing, Iran is bombing Israel and American bases in the other Arab countries of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait. But it is unlikely that Iran can sustain a war against the superior fire power of the United States and Israel.

A former CIA agent Dan Hoffman stated today on Fox News that the United States needs for the Iranian military to turn against the present regime. But he had little insight as to how this would happen. And it does not appear that the CIA has armed any Iranian factions to internally fight the military.

Hostilities will probably end in several weeks. But who knows? As generals who plan wars like to say, "We plan our attacks for months and we throw them out minutes after the war begins."

But President Trump may simply leave the present regime in power even when victorious. This is exactly what he did in Venezuela. After he removed Maduro, he made no attempt to replace the socialist Vice President. And it appears that Venezuela is slowly releasing political prisoners, stopping drug runs to the United States, diminishing the flow of illegals into the United States and allowing American oil companies to invest there.

Is it possible that a cowered Ayatollah will stop funding terrorism, trying to destroy Israel while abandoning its ballistic missile and nuclear agenda? Will they agree to allow inspections?

If President Trump neuters Iran, peace could break out in the Middle East and President Trump will deserve the Nobel Peace Prize each year for the next decade.

Or will Congressman Himes prediction be correct: "It does not appear that Donald Trump has learned the lessons of history."
Time will tell.

# [#]
I'm reaching out one last time before our February fundraising deadline closes at midnight tonight. Will you chip in $15 to help me hit my goal? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rr-em-fr-feb26?amount=15]

Four days ago, Trump used the State of the Union to double down on everything this administration has done in our communities and try to distract us from the consequences. No remorse. No limits. Just more of the same.

But we held the line. Democrats blocked funding for the department that includes ICE and demanded what any reasonable person would call common sense: that ICE agents get judicial warrants before entering people's homes, and that they stop concealing their identities with face masks when they show up in our neighborhoods, among other things.

Our communities deserve to feel safe. They deserve to know their rights. These protections matter.

That’s what I voted for, and it’s what I’ll keep fighting for.

And I know that puts a target on my back this November. Republicans are watching this district. They're going to come at us hard.

But I’m not backing down. I'm fighting for working families. For accessible healthcare. For the communities across CA-25 that sent me to Washington to be their voice — especially when it's hard.

This is one of those moments. And I can't do it without you.

Tonight is our last chance to close out February strong. Will you make a contribution of $15 or anything you can before tonight's midnight deadline? Every dollar counts. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rr-em-fr-feb26?amount=15]

Let's end this month ready to fight.

Peter,

Trump is gutting federal climate and public health protections. Earlier this month, his EPA repealed the _Endangerment Finding_ \- the legal foundation for nearly every major federal climate rule.

California has to step up. But right now, our own regulatory system is too slow and easy for corporate interests to stall, delay, and water down the laws we pass.

**So I introduced legislation to fix that.**

My bill cuts unnecessary red tape so we can move faster on state regulations that protect public health, our climate, and consumers - without corporate lobbyists tying them up in endless procedural delays.

[**Can I count on your support now to help get this done?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126355150/604718365/-1217084139?amount=10&refcode=SW_EM_FR_180DO_260228_2_4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDY5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MmU2OGQyOS1lNTE0LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=t2HSfYWJ_56ZIdsF6ITANVU4LcHY7AMx4QsHHr4CTd4=)

**We can’t afford that kind of delay - not on climate, not on public health, and especially not while federal protections are being torn down.**

I’m laying the groundwork to fix this first in California. Then, taking this fight all the way to Congress so we can act quickly to restore federal climate standards and health protections without losing years to procedural gridlock.

name: Mark Kelly
subject: War with Iran is illegal without a vote in Congress
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
It wasn’t long ago that thousands of American families lost sons and daughters to a war with no end in sight. Trump is risking that again with Iran, and he’s doing it all without Congressional approval.
#

People who’ve never served are often the quickest to start dropping bombs without a plan for what’s next.
The American people have seen this play out before and they’re tired of it. Trump is sending our servicemembers into harm’s way without a clear explanation or end goal.
It wasn’t long ago that thousands of American families lost sons and daughters to a war with no end in sight. Trump is risking that again with Iran, and he’s doing it all without Congressional approval.
The Senate needs to come back to Washington to do its job.
I am ready to vote on a War Powers Resolution. John Thune needs to call the Senate back for a vote, but that won’t happen unless we demand it.
[**Friend, please: Use this link and demand John Thune call the Senate back into session for a vote on a War Powers Resolution. name: Seth Moulton
subject: I’ve seen this before
body:
We cannot repeat the mistakes that cost American lives.

| |
---
Team, From the moment that news broke that Donald Trump ordered strikes on Iran, I could not help but think of the parallels to the Iraq War decades ago. Attacking a nation in the Middle East, putting thousands of American lives at risk, with no authorization, no plan, no briefing, and no strategy. Just another war built on lies. Peter , Right now, across the Middle East, young Americans in uniform are scanning the sky and bracing themselves, wondering if the next missile is the one that gets through. **Those missiles are incoming because Donald Trump unilaterally launched unprovoked and illegal strikes against Iran with no congressional authorization, and as his address and Truth Social posts made clear, no apparent cause beyond his own impulse.** In fact, just hours before the strikes, Oman's foreign minister announced that US-Iran peace talks had brought a deal within reach. Trump bombed anyway and now our troops are in grave danger. [**Help me get to Congress so there 's a veteran in that building who will actually say enough is enough.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt88pR62FECqq4LMqF3WsqdHEdjw4PAzsG0vuksJEJViE9qWm1BEjD0VWuOdE_Dee5kt_ViYRcB3x3gLd8euGuZspgPT1GVnj3KProHgk1WtpiH-cQyhKOk8ozP-r-9QEcx7mUR2dyKr6P4oaFiUX9JmKi61UDfjfwtISAiDNorrl0f4-Ee1qCdBYTH7Fwqa_vIjV7cj-4eHPw-pTgDMd56qOTP0oBw5ZnwjiuwBhl075_dfMLT91Aig2d6PZljTXbUH7_qW_K57Vq8SADqBGsY3jyPV4LnTP3CbHI3fzvrJVz/4oj/Yt9BHhxWQa-r-uwtY-OLWA/h1/h001.q3zCqdaYzQPFuSAjysWumRYn-uvX8udzIRZQpuSPqm8) As a combat aviator, I know what it feels like to be the instrument of a decision made by someone far away in a room you will never enter. I know the weight of that. I know what it costs. The loudest voices right now are wrapping themselves in the flag and cheering. **I am asking you to consider that the most deeply patriotic thing any of us can do at this moment is refuse to join that chorus.** Because real patriotism is not chest-thumping while someone else's kids take the incoming fire. Real patriotism is demanding that Congress honor the war powers our founding fathers enshrined in the Constitution precisely because they knew this moment would come. Keith Self recited the same oath I recited when I put on this uniform. He said those words twice, once in uniform and once when voters sent him to Congress. **Every syllable of that oath is a promise to a Constitution that could not be clearer: the power to take this country to war belongs to Congress. ** He has that power today to help stop this, while those young Americans are scanning a missile-filled sky and wondering if they are about to become another lost generation in another endless Middle East war. **He is doing absolutely nothing with it.** [**For every soldier under fire right now, chip in and help me flip this seat to replace Keith Self with a combat veteran who remembers what he swore to defend.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt88pR62FECqq4LMqF3WsqdHEdjw4PAzsG0vuksJEJViE9UdJluKy648D91i1eCI6oaGaRUOPqPT8KEjtT3JLjuBFEa6bMQ3k_2tdUFcenYbMzQfx7eJU5F8Ww2J4rxjP5AJwJU-EEJjykTJBMJ9ZIZRXayH2w26UqXelLAYQycsmp5n2CGq_MyVgzJMkD3DDLUejcqNUmWMnQzlkhQvBCb8WhsF6MyCleFSF10CHER0PmVpbwajkbSffeuyD219Gw9UCV3wkOHZrSo7m6hz6KeFs1bsgG0QDK0oS6x_ZVhxKg/4oj/Yt9BHhxWQa-r-uwtY-OLWA/h2/h001.-5FgqP_kodbPhWt-xR8iWIWmIYGdnL6sLWhPPxJf_K8) Very respectfully, Evan Hunt Candidate for U.S. Congress TX-03

In the quiet of last Sunday a SubStack post began its rapid ascent across X. It amassed tens of millions of views. By Monday's market open, the repercussions were visceral.
Shares of IBM **[plunged 13 percent,](https://substack.com/redirect/b869c2e5-6e63-42bf-8289-2db350c42221?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** marking the company's worst single-day performance since 2000. Credit-card giants Visa, Mastercard, and American Express shed between 4 and 8 percent of their value. DoorDash, Uber, Blackstone, and KKR followed with drops of up to 8 percent or more. **[Hundreds of billions were erased](https://substack.com/redirect/e7c37ce8-c069-4d20-a0bf-d3dcceb9d3df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from their market capitalizations, with payments companies alone reportedly losing around $100 billion.
The spark was not a disappointing earnings report or ominous Federal Reserve signals. It was a speculative thought experiment from **[Citrini Research entitled"The 2028 Global Intelligence Crisis."](https://substack.com/redirect/ab782ea3-a5b2-445d-8b41-6035d74738d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d633034d-bab7-4db7-87a2-43b260b76a8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Framed as a historical memo from June 30th, in 2028, the fictional report painted a picture of an economy where artificial intelligence had succeeded beyond all expectations--only to unravel the consumer-driven system that had powered the ascent of humankind. "AI didn't disappoint," the memo opened provocatively. "It exceeded every expectation. What happened?"
At its core, Citrini's scenario describes a vicious negative feedback loop. Advanced AI agents, capable of autonomous action, begin displacing white-collar workers en masse starting in late 2025. These high-earning professionals, who disproportionately drive discretionary spending in the economy, see their incomes evaporate or compress as they are forced to compete in gig economies. Consumer spending collapses.
Corporations, flush with higher margins from expanding AI at the cost of workers jobs, pour even more money into AI development, accelerating the displacement. The result is "Ghost GDP"--economic output registered in corporate ledgers and productivity statistics but failing to circulate as human demand for goods, services, restaurants, travel, and housing, because machines do not buy lattes or lease apartments.
In this speculative piece unemployment climbs to 10.2 percent, the S&P 500 falls 38 percent from its 2026 highs, private credit markets seize amid software company defaults, and even prime mortgages in tech hubs like San Francisco begin to crack as incomes falter.
What made this narrative so potent was not its inevitability but its unflinching focus on the demand side of the AI equation. Citrini and co-author Alap Shah explicitly called it a scenario exercise, an exploration of "left tail risks" rather than a forecast, but that nuance didn't matter to the 27 million people who read it.
For months, markets have been fixated on the supply side of AI: explosive capital expenditures on chips, data centers, bigger models, more compute, and relentlessly higher valuations. NVIDIA's valuation soared on the promise of AI infrastructure. Hyperscalers announced trillion-dollar data center build-outs. The prevailing narrative was one of boundless productivity and corporate profitability.
Labor-market consequences were often mentioned only in passing, usually as "creative destruction" or "upskilling opportunities." Citrini flipped the lens.
Citrini dared to ask: Who will buy the output if the buyers are unemployed or underemployed? It asked whether the bullish case on AI capability could itself be bearish for the economy. "What if our AI bullishness continues to be right," the preface wondered, "and what if that's actually bearish?" The market, apparently, had not priced that conditional. On Monday, it did, all at once.
The list of industries affected is all encompassing.
Intermediation businesses, those companies that act to smooth the friction generated by humans and businesses interacting, are in the crosshairs first.
Payment platforms, think credit card companies, will be bypassed by AI agentic commerce doing business through stablecoins in seconds.
Delivery platforms, like Uber Eats and DoorDash, will be fragmented by AI agents haggling directly with restaurant's AI agents over the price of your combination fried rice and spring rolls. A delivery that will show up on your door in an autonomous self driving car driven by, yes you guessed it, an AI agent.
Software as a Service subscriptions, think Zoom, **[Monday.com](https://substack.com/redirect/7da49f87-d318-4108-a12d-02a37fb38459?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and any one of a million "business productivity suites" will die because who needs collaboration software when there are barely any employees to collaborate with.
All these companies and many more not mentioned face existential compression as "zero-friction" AI eliminates human habits that have been the bedrock of the white collar world for a quarter century. The "pain points" of business will be fixed in moments by removing the weakest and most inef`icient link in the chain, the human. This may be great for productivity, but what do we do with all the humans?
This wasn't mere Luddite panic. It resonated because it echoed emerging data points. According to a **[2025 Pew Research Center survey](https://substack.com/redirect/3eafac59-b3fb-4fc1-9ab5-32ae8147e997?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , 52 percent of U.S. workers are worried about AI's future impact on their jobs, with 32 percent believing it will lead to fewer opportunities. McKinsey Global Institute research **[projects that](https://substack.com/redirect/1c6a7584-c1ec-4daa-a499-fb5caa1ebe30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** activities accounting for up to 30 percent of work hours in the U.S. economy could be automated by 2030, accelerating occupational shifts. The World Economic Forum **[estimates](https://substack.com/redirect/e409fec8-a4a8-4cc6-8593-9110ae247ed6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that AI and automation could displace 92 million jobs globally by 2030 while creating 170 million new ones, for a net gain of 78 million--_**but with 39 percent of core skills requiring change.**_
The market's violent reaction--described by some as an "AI scare trade"--underscored a deeper truth: Wall Street has been salivating over AI capex numbers for months while largely ignoring the potential macroeconomic feedback from labor-market transformation.
Legacy tech like IBM, reliant on services and mainframe modernization, symbolized vulnerability. Delivery and payments firms, built on human-centric models, saw the moats that have protected their profits for nearly five decades questioned. As one widely shared X thread noted, "just five paragraphs on AI agents transacting via stablecoins and bypassing interchange fees appeared to wipe out roughly $100 billion across credit-card stocks alone."
The backlash was swift, by Wednesday the pushback arrived, as it always does when a narrative threatens consensus. Critics dismissed it as a "scary bedtime story" with shaky economics. They pointed to historical precedents --from the steam engines to computers--where new technology leads to productivity surges and eventually fuels higher living standards and new demand pathways.
Citadel Securities, one of the world's largest market makers, **[published a point-by-point rebuttal](https://substack.com/redirect/0d21502a-3f3d-4a73-b3fb-b128420d0508?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** titled "The 2026 Global Intelligence Crisis." citing real-time labor data:
* AI adoption rates remain stable with no non-linear inflection,
* Software-engineering job postings are up 11 percent year-over-year,
* New business formation is expanding rapidly,
* Construction hiring is buoyed by data-center build outs .

They emphasized that technology diffusion follows S-curves. That organizational inertia and regulation act as brakes, and the elasticity of human desires has always absorbed efficiency gains--echoing Keynes's 1930 prediction of a 15-hour workweek that underestimated how expanded wants would sustain consumption.
The rebuttal was thorough, data-rich, and institutionally weighty. Yet its very existence underscored the anxiety it sought to dispel. When a major liquidity provider feels compelled to counter a fictional "scary bedtime story" on a SubStack, it signals that the underlying anxieties are probably not fringe. A scenario dismissed as "idiotic" by some traders still moved billions because enough participants feared it might contain a kernel of truth, suggesting that the boundary between fiction and financial reality has already blurred.
Investor psychology is fragile; a narrative that garnered more than 27 million views and that "felt true" moved real capital on Monday and wiped out billions. The scare is being minimized as unfounded, yet the fact that powerhouse firms feel compelled to prove that fact, only heightens the sense that the underlying dynamics could, under certain conditions, prove uncomfortably close to the mark.
Real-world evidence, meanwhile, sits in uneasy tension with the optimists. A January 2026 Harvard Business Review **[survey](https://substack.com/redirect/ceff6a23-3b0d-4338-8ce4-be8af90c557d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of 1,006 global executives found that 60 percent had already made headcount reductions to some degree explicitly in anticipation of AI's impact--and that was before the technology had delivered commensurate productivity gains.
Stanford's Digital Economy Lab documented a 13 percent employment decline since late 2022 among workers aged 22-25 in AI-exposed roles--the **["canaries in the coal mine."](https://substack.com/redirect/19ab62eb-ba26-4df7-af3b-43cc93d35c6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** A Reuters/Ipsos **[poll](https://substack.com/redirect/02338862-956c-40c3-a213-a91f7f450ed4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from August 2025 showed 71 percent of Americans worried that AI would permanently displace too many workers.
Even OpenAI's Sam Altman acknowledged in February 2026 that some companies were engaging in "AI washing," blaming layoffs on the technology when other factors were at play, while also conceding that **[genuine displacement was coming.](https://substack.com/redirect/fb977e33-2633-4908-990e-14e5e2cc0416?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/fb977e33-2633-4908-990e-14e5e2cc0416?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This episode invites a nuanced reckoning. AI's trajectory may not lead to the precise 2028 cataclysm Citrini laid out, but the speed and scope of which "intelligence abundance" is going to become real, challenges traditional models of economic adaptation. Put plainly, businesses are well known for not adapting to situations as quickly as they should and the AI future is moving faster than anything we have ever dealt with before.
White-collar jobs, once thought insulated, represent over half of employment and the bulk of high-value consumption. Unlike past automation waves targeting routine manual labor, AI targets cognitive tasks, potentially compressing or erasing the "intelligence premium" that underpins the middle class.
The broader implications extend beyond markets to culture and policy.
Work provides not just income but identity and purpose; a "Ghost Economy" risks hollowing out societal fabric. Democracy could strain under inequality exacerbated by AI. Policymakers must grapple with ideas floated in such scenarios: AI compute taxes, expanded direct transfers, massive re-skilling initiatives, or experiments in universal basic services.
Education systems need reinvention to foster uniquely human skills--creativity, empathy, complex problem-solving--that complement rather than compete with machines in a fight they are destined to lose. Businesses face choices: deploy AI for augmentation and value creation or pure cost-cutting that destroys their own customer base.
The Citrini report, in its provocative way, performs a public service by widening the aperture of debate. It reminds us that technology is not destiny; it is shaped by choices. As we stand on the cusp of potentially transformative AI capabilities, the real intelligence test is whether we can foresee and mitigate the dislocations while harnessing the abundance.
History suggests resilience and adaptation, but the velocity of which "the future" is traveling to meet us means that passive optimism may prove insufficient. The ghost in the machine economy is not inevitable obsolescence, but the specter of failing to align technological progress with human prosperity.
How we respond--to the hype, the hazards, and the opportunities--will define not just market cycles, but the contours of 21st-century society.

A scenario dismissed as "idiotic" by some traders still moved billions because enough participants feared it might contain a kernel of truth, suggesting that the boundary between fiction and financial reality has already blurred. Investor psychology is fragile; a narrative that garnered more than 27 million views and that "felt true" moved real capital on Monday and wiped out billions. The scare is being minimized as unfounded, yet the fact that powerhouse firms feel compelled to prove that fact, only heightens the sense that the underlying dynamics could, under certain conditions, prove uncomfortably close to the mark. Real-world evidence, meanwhile, sits in uneasy tension with the optimists. A January 2026 Harvard Business Review of 1,006 global executives found that 60 percent had already made headcount reductions to some degree explicitly in anticipation of AI's impact--and that was before the technology had delivered commensurate productivity gains. Stanford's Digital Economy Lab documented a 13 percent employment decline since late 2022 among workers aged 22-25 in AI-exposed roles--the A Reuters/Ipsos from August 2025 showed 71 percent of Americans worried that AI would permanently displace too many workers. Even OpenAI's Sam Altman acknowledged in February 2026 that some companies were engaging in "AI washing," blaming layoffs on the technology when other factors were at play, while also conceding that This episode invites a nuanced reckoning. AI's trajectory may not lead to the precise 2028 cataclysm Citrini laid out, but the speed and scope of which "intelligence abundance" is going to become real, challenges traditional models of economic adaptation. Put plainly, businesses are well known for not adapting to situations as quickly as they should and the AI future is moving faster than anything we have ever dealt with before. White-collar jobs, once thought insulated, represent over half of employment and the bulk of high-value consumption. Unlike past automation waves targeting routine manual labor, AI targets cognitive tasks, potentially compressing or erasing the "intelligence premium" that underpins the middle class. The broader implications extend beyond markets to culture and policy. Work provides not just income but identity and purpose; a "Ghost Economy" risks hollowing out societal fabric. Democracy could strain under inequality exacerbated by AI. Policymakers must grapple with ideas floated in such scenarios: AI compute taxes, expanded direct transfers, massive re-skilling initiatives, or experiments in universal basic services. Education systems need reinvention to foster uniquely human skills--creativity, empathy, complex problem-solving--that complement rather than compete with machines in a fight they are destined to lose. Businesses face choices: deploy AI for augmentation and value creation or pure cost-cutting that destroys their own customer base. The Citrini report, in its provocative way, performs a public service by widening the aperture of debate. It reminds us that technology is not destiny; it is shaped by choices. As we stand on the cusp of potentially transformative AI capabilities, the real intelligence test is whether we can foresee and mitigate the dislocations while harnessing the abundance. History suggests resilience and adaptation, but the velocity of which "the future" is traveling to meet us means that passive optimism may prove insufficient. The ghost in the machine economy is not inevitable obsolescence, but the specter of failing to align technological progress with human prosperity. How we respond--to the hype, the hazards, and the opportunities--will define not just market cycles, but the contours of 21st-century society. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.
